title: Communication and Responses
text: Use 115200 baud for the serial connection, or a TCP connection to the configured Ethernet IP address and port. Send one command per line, terminated by LF ( \n ). CRLF is also accepted. Command names and parameter letters are case-sensitive. Separate parameters with spaces. Angle brackets in usage descriptions are placeholders; do not send the brackets. M315 , M317 , M318 , and M319 process only the first option on a line. Send separate commands to change several settings. Most setting commands return Ok . Queries return their data without a trailing Ok . M312 returns Ok when the position move finishes, rather than immediately. Wait for the expected response before sending the next command. The firmware does not queue position moves. Serial lines are limited to 128 printable characters . An oversized line is discarded and returns Unknown:UART line too long! . Examples show commands and responses separately. Values in response examples are illustrative unless identified as the firmware version or date.

title: Detect Desktop Conveyor COM Port
text: Send IsXConveyor to identify the conveyor controller. Usage IsXConveyor Response YesXConveyor The same firmware also recognizes IsXEncoder and replies with YesXEncoder .

title: Firmware Information
text: Usage FirmwareVersion Date Responses for this firmware FirmwareVersion:1.1.3 FirmwareDate:27/10/2026

title: Device Address
text: Read the stored device address with Address , or set it with Address:<value> . The address is a 16-bit unsigned value ( 0 ? 65535 ) and is saved to nonvolatile memory. It is a device identifier, not the Ethernet IP address or TCP port; commands do not need an address prefix. Set an address Address:1 Response: Ok . Read the address Address Example response: Address:1

title: M310 - Set Motion Mode
text: Select how the motor pins are used. Usage M310 <mode> Mode Function 0 Output-pin mode. Use M314 to set the motor pin levels directly. 1 Position mode. Use M312 to move and M313 to set the move speed. 2 Velocity mode. Use M311 to set the speed and direction. 3 Potentiometer mode. The onboard potentiometer sets speed and direction. This is not a button-control mode. Changing to a different mode stops the current motion and resets the motor’s position to zero. Sending the mode that is already active leaves the position unchanged. The selected mode is saved to nonvolatile memory. Example M310 1 Response: Ok .

title: M311 - Set Speed In Velocity Mode
text: Set the target speed in mm/s. Positive and negative values select opposite directions; 0 requests a stop. Speed changes and direction reversals use the configured acceleration. Use M310 2 for serial/TCP velocity control. In mode 3 , the firmware also accepts M311 , but the next potentiometer update replaces the requested speed. In other modes, the speed request is ignored even though the command returns Ok . Usage M311 <speed> Example M311 200 Response: Ok . This acknowledges the command; it does not mean the target speed has already been reached.

title: M312 - Set Position
text: Move to an absolute motor position in mm, measured from the origin established at startup or the last change of motion mode. The target is not a relative distance from the current position. The conveyor must be in position mode ( M310 1 ) and have no position move in progress. Set the move speed with M313 before starting. A request made in another mode or during an active position move is ignored without a completion response. Usage M312 <position> Example M312 123 Response: Ok when the move finishes. If the target is already the current position, Ok is returned immediately. Sending M310 1 again while already in position mode does not reset the origin.

title: M313 - Set Speed In Position Move
text: Set the speed, in mm/s, for subsequent M312 moves. The firmware uses the absolute value of the supplied speed; direction comes from the target position. Usage M313 <speed> Example M313 300 Response: Ok . This speed setting is not saved to nonvolatile memory.

title: M314 - Set Motor Pins Level
text: An alternate function of the motor pins, available only in output-pin mode ( M310 0 ). This command is not used for normal conveyor motion. Usage M314 P<pin> V<level> Parameter Values P<pin> 0 : pulse pin (PUL); 1 : direction pin (DIR); 2 : enable pin (EN). V<level> 0 : LOW; 1 : HIGH. Keep the parameter order P then V . Response: Ok . In other motion modes, the pins are not changed even though Ok is returned.

title: M315 - Config Conveyor Parameters
text: Read the conveyor configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage M315 M315 S<pulses_per_mm> M315 R<reverse> M315 E<enable> M315 P M315 A<acceleration> Option Function No option Read mode, motor pulses/mm, and direction reversal. S<value> Set motor pulses/mm to match the motor and transmission. Use a positive calibrated value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. E<value> Store the run-with-encoder flag ( 0 or 1 ). In firmware 1.1.3 this flag is not used by the motion-control loop; it does not enable closed-loop positioning. P Stop an active position move immediately and update the estimated motor position from the pulses sent so far. It does not take a target position. A<value> Set acceleration in mm/s?. The firmware uses the absolute value. S , R , E , and A are saved to nonvolatile memory. Setting commands return Ok . The B parameter from X Conveyor is not implemented here. Example: change settings separately M315 S31.83 M315 R0 M315 A5000 The numbers above are examples, not factory calibration values. Example response to M315 M:1 S:31.83 R:0 The query returns only M , S , and R ; it does not report acceleration or the encoder flag. After stopping a position move Use M315 P only during an active position move. Firmware 1.1.3 leaves the move counter set after this stop, so change to another mode and back before issuing a new M312 . Changing mode resets the motor position origin.
syntax: M315 M315 S<pulses_per_mm> M315 R<reverse> M315 E<enable> M315 P M315 A<acceleration>

title: M316 - Set Encoder Mode
text: Select the encoder reporting mode. Changing the setting clears the encoder position counters and saves the mode to nonvolatile memory. Usage M316 <mode> Mode Function 0 Absolute position since the last encoder reset. 1 Relative position change since the previous position report. 2 Use encoder channels A and B as input pins with M319 , instead of decoding encoder pulses. Button mode ( 3 ) is not implemented. Example M316 1 Response: Ok .

title: M317 - Get Position from Encoder
text: Read the position once, configure periodic position reports, or reset the encoder position. Use one option per command. Usage M317 M317 T<period_ms> M317 R Option Function No option Return one position report. T<value> Set the report period in milliseconds. Values from 50 to 65535 enable reporting; values below 50 , including 0 , stop it. R Reset the encoder position to zero. This does not reset the motor position used by M312 . Position values use the absolute or relative mode selected by M316 and have two decimal places. Query M317 Example response: P0:5.32 Enable periodic reports M317 T500 The command returns Ok , followed by P0:<position> reports every 500 ms. Send M317 T0 to stop reporting. Reset M317 R Response: Ok .

title: M318 - Set Encoder Parameters
text: Read the encoder configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage M318 M318 S<pulses_per_mm> M318 R<reverse> M318 C<scale> Option Function No option Read encoder mode, scale, pulses/mm, reversal, and report period. S<value> Set the calibrated pulses/mm for the selected scale. Use a positive value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. C<value> Select pulse-counting scale: 1 , 2 , or 4 . Each valid setting clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration. Changing C does not automatically adjust S ; set both in separate commands. Calibration is loaded from nonvolatile memory, so this reference does not assume a fixed factory pulses/mm value. Example M318 C2 M318 S10.24 M318 R1 Each setting returns Ok . The pulses/mm value above is an example calibration for scale 2 . Example response to M318 M:1 C:2 S:10.24 R:1 T:500
syntax: M318 M318 S<pulses_per_mm> M318 R<reverse> M318 C<scale>

title: M319 - Read Encoder Pin
text: Read channels A/B as digital inputs, or report changes to their states. Select input-pin mode with M316 2 first; these functions replace normal encoder pulse decoding. Usage M319 V<pin> M319 T<pin> M319 S<pin> Option Function V<pin> Read the current input state. T<pin> Enable reports when the input state changes. S<pin> Disable reports when the input state changes. Pin 0 is encoder channel A; pin 1 is channel B. Send one option per command. T and S return Ok ; V returns the pin state without a trailing Ok . Example M319 V1 Example response: I1 V1 Reports use I0 V<state> or I1 V<state> , where state is 0 or 1 .
syntax: M319 V<pin> M319 T<pin> M319 S<pin>

title: M389 - Enable Ethernet
text: Set the Ethernet startup-enable flag. M389 1 also initializes Ethernet immediately with the current configuration. Usage M389 <enable> 1 : set the enable flag and initialize Ethernet. 0 : clear the enable flag. In firmware 1.1.3, this does not close an already running Ethernet server or client connection. The flag is saved with M396 . That command also initializes Ethernet, even when the flag is 0 ; the disabled startup state takes effect after restarting the controller. Response: Ok . Ethernet initialization also sends status messages to the serial connection.

title: M390 - Set Ethernet Port
text: Set the TCP server port in the current configuration. Save and apply the setting with M396 . Usage M390 <port> Example M390 8844 Response: Ok . The source defines 8844 as the initial port, but startup loads the stored configuration. Use M397 to check the configured port.

title: M391 - Set Ethernet IP Address
text: Set the configured IPv4 address using four decimal octets. 0 0 0 0 selects DHCP when Ethernet is next initialized. Save and apply with M396 . Usage M391 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Static-IP example M391 192 168 0 2 DHCP M391 0 0 0 0 Each command returns Ok .

title: M392 - Set Ethernet DNS Address
text: Set the configured DNS address using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage M392 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example M392 192 168 0 1 Response: Ok .

title: M393 - Set Ethernet Gateway Address
text: Set the configured gateway using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage M393 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example M393 192 168 0 1 Response: Ok .

title: M394 - Set Ethernet Subnet Address
text: Set the configured subnet mask using four decimal octets. Save and apply with M396 . Usage M394 <octet1> <octet2> <octet3> <octet4> Example M394 255 255 255 0 Response: Ok .

title: M395 - Set Ethernet MAC Address
text: Set the MAC address using six decimal byte values from 0 to 255 , separated by spaces. Convert a hexadecimal MAC address to decimal before sending it. Save and apply with M396 . Usage M395 <byte1> <byte2> <byte3> <byte4> <byte5> <byte6> Example M395 18 52 86 120 171 5 This represents 12:34:56:78:AB:05 . Response: Ok .

title: M396 - Save and Init Ethernet Port
text: Save the current Ethernet settings and enable flag to nonvolatile memory, then initialize the Ethernet server with those settings. Usage M396 Configure network settings through the serial connection, since applying a new configuration can interrupt the TCP connection. M396 initializes Ethernet regardless of the enable flag; set M389 1 before saving if Ethernet should start automatically after a restart. Response: Ok . Initialization status is also printed on the serial connection.

title: M397 - Get Ethernet Port Parameters
text: Read the configured values held by the firmware. These may include changes that have not yet been saved or applied. Usage M397 Example response E_port:8844 E_ip:192.168.0.2 E_dns:192.168.0.1 E_gateway:192.168.0.1 E_subnet:255.255.255.0 E_mac:18.52.86.120.171.5 The MAC address is reported as decimal bytes separated by dots. There is no trailing Ok .

title: M398 - Get Ethernet Local Port Parameters
text: Read the network stack’s active IP, DNS, gateway, and subnet . The reported port and MAC fields come from the firmware’s configured values. Use this command after Ethernet initialization to check the assigned IP address, especially when using DHCP. Usage M398 The response uses the same fields as M397 , without a trailing Ok . With DHCP, the configured IP in M397 can be 0.0.0.0 while M398 shows the assigned IP address. The text command IP returns the same network information. When sent through TCP, IP also echoes a line containing IP before the fields; the serial response has no echo line.

Command names and parameter letters are case-sensitive. Separate parameters with spaces. Angle brackets in usage descriptions are placeholders; do not send the brackets. title: Reset Controller
text: Restart the controller with the case-sensitive text command Reset . This restarts the firmware; it does not restore factory configuration. Usage Reset The controller prints XConveyor Reset to the serial connection , even if the command was sent through TCP, then restarts after about 100 ms. There is no Ok response. Reconnect after the controller starts again.

title: I/O Pin Numbering
text: The four dedicated inputs/outputs use zero-based command indices. They are separate from the encoder channels and motor pins. Command index Dedicated input Dedicated output 0 Input 1 Output 1 1 Input 2 Output 2 2 Input 3 Output 3 3 Input 4 Output 4 Use M330 ? M333 for these dedicated I/O pins. M319 instead uses 0 / 1 for encoder channels A/B; M314 uses 0 / 1 / 2 for motor PUL/DIR/EN.

title: XConveyor
text: Motor control, dedicated digital I/O, and Ethernet configuration commands.

title: M310 - Set Motion Mode
text: Select the motor-control mode. Usage M310 <mode> Mode Function 0 Output-pin mode. Control motor PUL/DIR/EN directly with M314 . 1 Position mode. Use M312 to move and M313 to set the move speed. 2 Velocity mode. Use M311 to set speed and direction. 3 Input-control mode. Functions assigned with M332 can change speed, move a relative distance, or stop. Encoder-button control with M316 3 also requires this mode. Changing to a different mode stops motion and resets the motor position, input-speed target, and position-reached state. Resending the mode already active does not reset the motor position. The mode is saved to nonvolatile memory. Input mode also accepts M311 , subject to its motion-state restrictions. It is not potentiometer mode. Example M310 3 Response: Ok .

title: M311 - Set Speed In Velocity Mode
text: Set the signed target speed in mm/s. Positive and negative values select opposite directions; 0 requests a stop. Acceleration is applied to speed changes, and a direction reversal decelerates to zero before reversing. The command acts in velocity mode ( M310 2 ) or input mode ( M310 3 ). It does not interrupt an active position move. Requests in other modes or during a position move are ignored even though Ok is returned. Usage M311 <speed> Example M311 200 Response: Ok . This acknowledges the request, not that the target speed has been reached. The requested speed is limited by the motor pulse calibration and the maximum step rate: 20000 / pulses_per_mm in mm/s. This firmware limit is not the conveyor’s mechanical speed rating.

title: M312 - Set Position
text: Move to an absolute motor position in mm, referenced to startup or the last actual change of motion mode. This is different from the relative-distance input function M332 F3 . Use position mode ( M310 1 ) before sending this command. A new position target is not queued while a position move is already running. Usage M312 <position> Example M312 123 Response: Ok when the move finishes. If the target already equals the current position, Ok is returned immediately. A request ignored because of mode or motion state has no completion response. Set the move speed with M313 . Resending M310 1 while already in position mode does not reset the origin.

title: M313 - Set Speed In Position Move
text: Set the speed in mm/s for subsequent position moves, including relative moves triggered through M332 F3 . The absolute value is used and is limited to the maximum step rate for the configured motor pulses/mm. Usage M313 <speed> Example M313 300 Response: Ok . This setting is saved to nonvolatile memory in X Conveyor firmware 2.1.1. If no valid stored position speed is available at startup, the firmware uses 50 mm/s.

title: M314 - Set Motor Pins Level
text: An alternate function of the motor pins, available only in output-pin mode ( M310 0 ). This command is not used for normal conveyor motion. Usage M314 P<pin> V<level> Parameter Values P<pin> 0 : pulse pin (PUL); 1 : direction pin (DIR); 2 : enable pin (EN). V<level> 0 : LOW; 1 : HIGH. Keep the parameter order P then V . Response: Ok . In other motion modes, the pins are not changed even though Ok is returned.

title: M315 - Config Conveyor Parameters
text: Read the conveyor configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage M315 M315 S<pulses_per_mm> M315 R<reverse> M315 E<enable> M315 P M315 A<acceleration> M315 B<button_start_speed> Option Function No option Read mode, motor pulses/mm, and direction reversal. S<value> Set motor pulses/mm to match the motor and transmission. Use a positive calibrated value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. Configure this while the conveyor is stopped. E<value> Store the run-with-encoder flag ( 0 or 1 ). In firmware 2.1.1 it is not used by the motion-control loop and does not enable closed-loop positioning. P Stop an active position move immediately and update the estimated motor position from pulses already sent. It does not take a target position. A<value> Set acceleration in mm/s?. Use a nonnegative value; 0 requests speed changes without an acceleration ramp. B<value> Set the start speed used when holding encoder button A in M316 3 / M310 3 . This is not the speed step of the dedicated inputs configured with M332 . S , R , E , and A save the configuration to nonvolatile memory. B updates the button-start speed in RAM but does not itself save it. Setting commands return Ok . Example: send settings separately M315 S31.83 M315 R0 M315 A1000 These numbers are examples, not factory calibration values. Example response to M315 M:1 S:31.83 R:0 The query returns only M , S , and R ; acceleration, the encoder flag, and button-start speed are not included. Use M315 P during a position move. This firmware clears the move counter after the stop, so a subsequent M312 can start without changing mode or resetting the position origin.
syntax: M315 M315 S<pulses_per_mm> M315 R<reverse> M315 E<enable> M315 P M315 A<acceleration> M315 B<button_start_speed>

title: M330 - Set Output Pin
text: Set one of the four dedicated outputs. The output must have function F0 selected with M333 before it can be controlled manually. Usage M330 P<pin> V<state> Parameter Values P<pin> Output index 0 ? 3 , corresponding to Output 1?4. V<state> 0 : off; 1 : on. Keep the parameter order P then V . Example: manually activate Output 1 M333 P0 F0 M330 P0 V1 Each command returns Ok . If the output has an automatic function ( F1 or F2 ), M330 returns Unknown:Output has function! and leaves it under automatic control.

title: M331 - Read Input Pin
text: Read one of the four dedicated inputs, or enable/disable reports when its logic state changes. Send one option per command. Usage M331 V<pin> M331 T<pin> M331 S<pin> Option Function V<pin> Read the current input state. T<pin> Enable reports when the state changes. S<pin> Disable change reports. Use pin indices 0 ? 3 for Input 1?4. V returns data without Ok ; T and S return Ok . Automatic reporting is separate from the input’s assigned motion function and is not saved across restarts. Example: read Input 1 M331 V0 Example response: I0 V1 M331 T0 enables further I0 V<state> reports. M331 S0 stops them. These are raw logic-state changes, not the debounced motion triggers used by M332 .
syntax: M331 V<pin> M331 T<pin> M331 S<pin>

title: M332 - Configure Input Pin
text: Assign a motion function to a dedicated input. These functions are active only in input-control mode ( M310 3 ) . Pin indices are 0 ? 3 . Usage M332 M332 I<pin> M332 I<pin> F<function> V<value> No options: return the configuration of all four inputs. I<pin> alone: return that input’s configuration. I<pin> F<function> : set the function. Add V<value> to set the function value. Parameter order is flexible. Function Behavior Value F0 No motion function. Reading/reporting through M331 remains available. Ignored. F1 Increase the input controller’s speed target. Step in mm/s. F2 Decrease the input controller’s speed target. Step in mm/s. F3 Move by a relative distance from the current motor position. Signed distance in mm. F4 Stop an active position move immediately, or request zero velocity for a speed run. Ignored. A function triggers when the input logic becomes 1 after remaining stable for more than 25 ms . Holding F1 / F2 for more than 1.5 seconds repeats the speed step at approximately 100 ms intervals. F1 / F2 are ignored during a position move. F3 is accepted only when the conveyor is stopped with no pending reversal or position move, and uses the speed set by M313 . F4 handles both motion types in input mode. The input-speed target starts at zero when the motion mode changes. Example: assign speed-up to Input 1 and stop to Input 2 M332 I0 F1 V50 M332 I1 F4 V0 M310 3 Each setting returns Ok . Functions and values are saved to nonvolatile memory. Example response to M332 I0 I0 F1 V50.00 M332 without options returns one line per input, I0 through I3 , with no trailing Ok .
syntax: M332 M332 I<pin> M332 I<pin> F<function> V<value>

title: M333 - Configure Output Pin
text: Assign an automatic function to a dedicated output, or return it to manual control. These functions follow the firmware’s motor-motion state for both command-driven and input-triggered moves. They are not measurements of encoder-confirmed belt motion. Usage M333 M333 P<pin> M333 P<pin> F<function> V<value> Use output indices 0 ? 3 . Without options, read all outputs; with P<pin> alone, read one. Parameter order is flexible. Function Activation condition F0 Manual output controlled with M330 . F1 The controller’s position-reached flag is set after a completed position move or an already-reached M312 target. This is a maintained state, not a timed pulse. F2 V0 The nonzero requested velocity is reached during a velocity run. Does not activate for position moves or a zero-speed target. F2 V>0 Signed motor speed is greater than or equal to the positive forward threshold in mm/s. F2 V<0 Signed motor speed is less than or equal to the negative reverse threshold in mm/s. Signed threshold functions can operate during either velocity or position moves. A new move or a change of motion mode clears the position-reached flag. Example M333 P0 F1 V0 M333 P1 F2 V50 M333 P2 F2 V-50 Each setting returns Ok and is saved to nonvolatile memory. Assigning a function initially turns the output off; the next control update applies its activation condition. While F1 / F2 is assigned, manual M330 requests are rejected. Use M333 P0 F0 to return Output 1 to manual control. Example response to M333 P1 O1 F2 V50.00 Queries use the prefix O in their responses, even though the command selects the pin with P . The all-output query returns O0 through O3 , with no trailing Ok .
syntax: M333 M333 P<pin> M333 P<pin> F<function> V<value>

title: M389 - Enable Ethernet
text: Set the Ethernet startup-enable flag and save the current Ethernet configuration immediately . Usage M389 <enable> 1 : enable Ethernet at startup and initialize it immediately with the current configuration. 0 : disable Ethernet at the next startup. In firmware 2.1.1, this does not close an already running server or TCP client connection. Response: Ok . Initialization status and the assigned IP address are also printed on the serial connection when enabling Ethernet.

title: M392 - Set Ethernet DNS Address

title: M393 - Set Ethernet Gateway Address

title: M395 - Set Ethernet MAC Address
text: Set the MAC address using six decimal byte values from 0 to 255 , separated by spaces. Convert a hexadecimal MAC address to decimal before sending it. Save and apply with M396 . Usage M395 <byte1> <byte2> <byte3> <byte4> <byte5> <byte6> Example M395 18 52 86 120 171 5 This represents 12:34:56:78:AB:05 . Response: Ok .

title: M396 - Save and Init Ethernet Port
text: Save the current Ethernet settings and enable flag to nonvolatile memory, then initialize the server with those settings. Usage M396 Configure network settings through serial, since applying them can interrupt the TCP connection. This command initializes Ethernet even if its startup-enable flag is 0 ; it does not change that flag. Use M389 1 when Ethernet should also start automatically after a restart. Response: Ok . Initialization status and the assigned IP address are also printed on the serial connection.

title: M397 - Get Ethernet Port Parameters
text: Read the configured values held by the firmware. These may include changes that have not yet been saved or applied. Usage M397 Example response E_port:8844 E_ip:192.168.0.2 E_dns:192.168.0.1 E_gateway:192.168.0.1 E_subnet:255.255.255.0 E_mac:18.52.86.120.171.5 The MAC address is reported as decimal bytes separated by dots. There is no trailing Ok .

title: M398 - Get Ethernet Local Port Parameters
text: Read the network stack’s active IP, DNS, gateway, and subnet . The port and MAC fields come from the firmware’s current configured values. Usage M398 The response uses the same fields as M397 , without a trailing Ok . After DHCP initialization, M397 can show the configured IP as 0.0.0.0 , while M398 shows the assigned IP. The text command IP returns the same information over both serial and TCP, without an extra echo line.

title: M399 - Reset Ethernet Parameters
text: Restore the following network configuration, save it to nonvolatile memory, and immediately reinitialize Ethernet: Setting Reset value TCP port 8844 Configured IP 0.0.0.0 (DHCP) Configured DNS, gateway, subnet 0.0.0.0 MAC address DE:AD:BE:EF:FE:32 (decimal bytes 222.173.190.239.254.50 ) This command leaves the Ethernet startup-enable flag unchanged. It resets network settings only, not motor, encoder, or I/O configuration. Use the serial connection because the active TCP connection can be interrupted. Usage M399 Configuration response E_port:8844 E_ip:0.0.0.0 E_dns:0.0.0.0 E_gateway:0.0.0.0 E_subnet:0.0.0.0 E_mac:222.173.190.239.254.50 There is no trailing Ok . Initialization status is also printed on serial. Use M398 or IP afterward to read the active address assigned by DHCP.

title: XEncoder
text: Encoder position, pulse calibration, and channel input commands. When updating an earlier X Encoder integration: Position reports use P0:<position> , rather than the P:<position> examples in the old reference. Read or set encoder calibration with M318 ; do not assume the old reference’s 5.12 pulses/mm value applies to the current controller. For M319 , select M316 2 and specify channel 0 (A) or 1 (B), such as M319 V0 or M319 T1 . These channels replace encoder pulse decoding while used as inputs. The controller’s separate digital inputs use M331 .

title: M316 - Set Encoder Mode
text: Select how encoder channels A and B are used. Setting a mode clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration. Usage M316 <mode> Mode Function 0 Absolute encoder position since the last reset. 1 Relative position change since the previous position report. 2 Digital input mode for channels A/B, queried with M319 . 3 Button mode on channels A/B. Motion control also requires M310 3 . Encoder-button behavior in mode 3 The firmware treats a channel’s HIGH logic state as pressed: Channel A active for more than 150 ms increases the button-speed target by 5 mm/s. Held for more than 2 seconds, it sets the target to the start speed configured by M315 B . Channel B active for more than 150 ms decreases the button-speed target by 5 mm/s. Held for more than 2 seconds, it requests zero speed. These button actions request velocity changes and do not interrupt an active position move. Use a dedicated input with M332 F4 to stop either type of motion in input mode. Button mode replaces encoder pulse decoding. It is separate from the four dedicated input functions configured with M332 . Example M316 1 Response: Ok .

title: M317 - Get Position from Encoder
text: Read the position once, configure periodic position reports, or reset the encoder position. Use one option per command. Usage M317 M317 T<period_ms> M317 R Option Function No option Return one position report. T<value> Set the report period in milliseconds. Values from 50 to 65535 enable reporting; values below 50 , including 0 , stop it. R Reset the encoder position to zero. This does not reset the motor position used by M312 . Position values use the absolute or relative mode selected by M316 and have two decimal places. Query M317 Example response: P0:5.32 Enable periodic reports M317 T500 The command returns Ok , followed by P0:<position> reports every 500 ms. Send M317 T0 to stop reporting. Reset M317 R Response: Ok .

title: M318 - Set Encoder Parameters
text: Read the encoder configuration or change one setting per command . Additional options on the same line are ignored. Usage M318 M318 S<pulses_per_mm> M318 R<reverse> M318 C<scale> Option Function No option Read encoder mode, scale, pulses/mm, reversal, and report period. S<value> Set the calibrated pulses/mm for the selected scale. Use a positive value. R<value> 0 : normal direction; 1 : reverse direction. C<value> Select pulse-counting scale: 1 , 2 , or 4 . Each valid setting clears the encoder position counters and saves the configuration. Changing C does not automatically adjust S ; set both in separate commands. Calibration is loaded from nonvolatile memory, so this reference does not assume a fixed factory pulses/mm value. Example M318 C2 M318 S10.24 M318 R1 Each setting returns Ok . The pulses/mm value above is an example calibration for scale 2 . Example response to M318 M:1 C:2 S:10.24 R:1 T:500
syntax: M318 M318 S<pulses_per_mm> M318 R<reverse> M318 C<scale>

title: M319 - Read Encoder Pin
text: Read channels A/B as digital inputs, or report changes to their states. Select input-pin mode with M316 2 first; these functions replace normal encoder pulse decoding. Usage M319 V<pin> M319 T<pin> M319 S<pin> Option Function V<pin> Read the current input state. T<pin> Enable reports when the input state changes. S<pin> Disable reports when the input state changes. Pin 0 is encoder channel A; pin 1 is channel B. Send one option per command. T and S return Ok ; V returns the pin state without a trailing Ok . Send one command per line, terminated by LF ( \n ). CRLF is also accepted. Command names and parameter letters are case-sensitive. Separate parameters with spaces. title: Communication and Responses
text: Connect at 115200 baud , with 8 data bits, no parity, and 1 stop bit . Send one command per line, ending with a newline ( \n ) . CRLF is also accepted for the numeric commands below. Use uppercase command names, starting at the beginning of the line, followed by a space and a numeric value: M311 50 . Values are positional: use M311 50 , not M311 S50 . These commands are setters, not queries; always provide a value. Missing or nonnumeric values can be parsed as zero. The controller prints Begin: at startup and starts in potentiometer mode . The knob can therefore start the belt after power-on or reset. M310 , M311 , and M313 reply with Ok immediately. A nonzero M312 normally replies with Ok when its move completes. Settings are held in RAM and return to startup defaults after a reset. There is no save-to-memory command. This firmware implements M310, M311, M312, and M313 only . It does not implement IsXConveyor , encoder feedback, general-purpose input/output commands, or Ethernet commands. Unsupported commands do not produce an error reply.

title: Quick Start
text: Send each line separately and wait for its Ok reply before continuing. Select serial control: text M310 1 Run continuously at 50 mm/s: text M311 50 Stop continuous motion: text M311 0 For a relative position move, set the position speed with M313 , then send M312 and wait for its completion reply.

title: M310 - Select Control Mode
text: Select whether the potentiometer or serial commands control the conveyor. Usage M310 <mode> Parameters Parameter Description 0 Potentiometer mode, the startup default. The knob controls speed from 0 to 200 mm/s in one direction. 1 Serial mode. Use M311 for continuous motion and M312 for relative moves. The potentiometer is ignored in serial mode. Selecting serial mode sets the continuous speed request to zero; it does not clear an active position move. Select M310 1 before sending serial movement commands. In potentiometer mode, those commands do not immediately drive the motor, even when a command returns Ok . Example M310 1 Response: Ok . Switch modes only after a position move has completed. Returning to M310 0 lets the current knob setting control the belt again.

title: M311 - Set Continuous Speed
text: Run continuously at a signed speed, or stop continuous motion. Requires serial mode ( M310 1 ). Usage M311 <speed> Parameters Parameter Description <speed> Speed in mm/s. Positive and negative values select opposite directions. 0 stops continuous motion. The firmware limits the speed magnitude to 200 mm/s . A magnitude below 0.01 mm/s is treated as zero. It changes the step timing directly, without an acceleration ramp. Examples Run at 50 mm/s: M311 50 Run in the opposite direction: M311 -50 Stop continuous motion: M311 0 Each command replies with Ok . This acknowledges the command; it is not measured speed feedback. M311 0 does not cancel an active M312 position move. Wait for that move to finish before using continuous-speed commands.

title: M312 - Move Relative Distance
text: Move a signed distance from the current belt position, then stop. Requires serial mode ( M310 1 ). Set the movement speed with M313 . Usage M312 <distance> Parameters Parameter Description <distance> Relative distance in mm. Positive and negative values select opposite directions. This is not an absolute position or a homing command. The firmware converts distance to steps using 84 steps/mm , rounded to the nearest whole step. Position is calculated from commanded motor steps; there is no encoder verification. Direction convention In this firmware, positive M312 moves in the opposite direction to positive M311 . Negative values also have opposite direction conventions between the two commands. Example From a stopped conveyor in serial mode, set a position speed of 30 mm/s and wait for Ok : M313 30 Move 100 mm and wait for the completion Ok : M312 100 Move 100 mm in the opposite direction: M312 -100 Completion and Sequencing For a nonzero move, Ok is sent when the requested step count completes. The firmware then stops the step timer and disables the motor driver. M312 0 returns Ok immediately, but does not cancel a move that is already running. There is no motion queue or position-move cancellation command. Wait for completion before sending another motion, mode, or position-speed command; commands sent during a move can modify its active step count, direction, or speed. Very small nonzero distances can round to zero steps and produce no completion reply . One step is approximately 0.0119 mm ; use distances of at least one step for normal positioning.

title: M313 - Set Position Move Speed
text: Set the speed used by M312 . The startup default is 30 mm/s . Configure this while the conveyor is stopped, before starting a position move. Usage M313 <speed> Parameters Parameter Description <speed> Positive position-move speed in mm/s. Use a value no greater than 200 mm/s. Direction is selected by the sign of M312 , not by this value. The firmware assigns this value directly: it does not validate or clamp M313 like it does M311 . Do not use zero or negative values. This setting is lost after reset. Example M313 40 Response: Ok . Subsequent M312 moves use 40 mm/s. M313 does not specify a distance and does not start a move from idle.

Set the feed rate with F once. Subsequent movement commands use that feed rate until you change it; you do not need to repeat F in every movement command. Usage G00 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] G01 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] Parameters F[rate]

title: G00, G01 - Linear Move
text: Descriptions The G0 and G1 commands add a LINEAR MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage G00 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] G01 [F<rate>] [A<rate>] [J<rate>] [S<rate>] [E<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] Parameters F[rate] : (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[rate] : (mm/s^2) The maximum acceleration of the movement. J[rate] : (mm/s^3) The jerk of the movement. S[rate] : (mm/s) The start velocity of the movement. E[rate] : (mm/s) The end velocity of the movement. X[pos] : (mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] : (mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] : (mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] : (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. U[angle] : (mm) A coordinate on the 5-axis. Example G01 X12 ;move to 12mm on the X-axis G01 F200 ;set the feedrate to 200 mm/s G01 X90.6 Y13.8 ;move to 90.6mm on the X-axis and 13.8mm on the Y-axis G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G01 W90 ;rotate to 90 degree on the 4-axis G01 X100 Y50 Z-400 W90 U45 F200 ;X=100 mm, Y=50 mm, Z=-400 mm, W=90°, U=45°, F=200 mm/s

title: G02, G03 - Arc or Circle Move
text: Descriptions G2 adds a clockwise arc move to the planner; G3 adds a counter-clockwise arc. An arc move starts at the current position and ends at the given XYZ, pivoting around a center-point offset given by I and J. Usage G2 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] G3 [F<rate>] [I<offset>] [J<offset>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] Parameters F[rate] : (mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. I[offset] :(mm) An offset from the current X position to use as the arc center. J[offset] :(mm) An offset from the current Y position to use as the arc center. X[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] : (mm) A coordinate on the 4-axis. U[angle] : (mm) A coordinate on the 5-axis. Example G28 G01 Z-350 G01 X50 G02 X-50 Y0 I-50 J0 G03 X50 Y0 I50 J0

title: G04 - Dwell/Delay
text: Descriptions Dwell pauses the command queue and waits for a period of time. Usage G04 [P<time>] Parameters P[time]: delay time in miliseconds. Example G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 G4 P500 ;delay 500ms G01 X100

title: G05 - Bézier cubic spline
text: Descriptions G5 creates a cubic B-spline in the XY plane with the X and Y axes only. P and Q parameters are required . I and J are required for the first G5 command in a series . For subsequent G5 commands, either both I and J must be specified , or neither. Usage G5 [F<rate>] I<pos> J<pos> P<pos> Q<pos> X<pos> Y<pos> Parameters F[rate] :(mm/s) The maximum feedrate of the move between the start and end point. This value applies to all subsequent moves. I[offset] :(mm) Offset from the X start point to first control point. J[offset] :(mm) Offset from the Y start point to first control point. P[offset] :(mm) Offset from the X end point to second control point. Q[offset] :(mm) Offset from the Y end point to the second control point. X[pos] :(mm) A destination coordinate on the X axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A destination coordinate on the Y axis. Example ;program a curvy “N” shape G0 X0 Y0 G5 I0 J3 P0 Q-3 X1 Y1
syntax: G5 [F<rate>] I<pos> J<pos> P<pos> Q<pos> X<pos> Y<pos>

title: G06 - Theta angle control
text: Descriptions Directly control movement angle without endpoint coordinates. Usage G06 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] Parameters X[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. Example G6 X0 Y0 Z0 ;set theta 1, theta 2, theta 3 angle at 0 deg

title: G28 - Homing
text: Descriptions Auto-home all axes, moving them towards their endstops until triggered. Usage G28

title: G90 - Absolute Movement Mode
text: Descriptions In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage G90 Note Absolute positioning is the default.

title: G91 - Relative Movement Mode
text: Descriptions Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage G91 Example G91 ; Set all axes to relative

title: G93 - Get Current Position
text: Descriptions Get current position of end effector. Usage G93 Feedback <xpos>, <ypos>, <zpos> <xpos> : Current X position. <ypos> : Current Y position. <zpos> : Current Z position. Example G93 ; get current pos return: 31, 43, -270

title: M03 - Vacuum On / Gripper Close
text: Descriptions M03 is used to turn on the vacuum pump or close the gripper. Usage M03 Example G01 X0 Y0 Z-350 M03 ;turn on Vacuum pump G01 Z-300

title: M04 - Turn on digital output pins
text: Descriptions M04 is used to turn on and set PWM value for digital output pin (D0 - D3). Usage M04 [D<pin>] [P<value>] Parameters D[pin] :(0 ~ 3) The index of output pin P[value] :(0 - 255) The value of the pwm Example M04 D1 P128 ;set pin D1 pwm at 50%

title: M05 - Vacuum Off / Gripper Open
text: Descriptions M05 is used to turn off the vacuum pump or close the gripper. Usage M05 ;turn off vacuum

title: M06 - Turn off digital output pins
text: Descriptions M06 is used to turn off digital output pin (D0 - D3). Usage M06 [D<pin>] Parameters D[pin] :(0 ~ 3) The index of output pin Example M06 D1 ;turn off pin D1

title: M07 - Read Input Signals
text: Descriptions M07 is used to read the input signal from the input pins. Usage M07 [I<pin>] [A<pin>] Parameters I[pin] :(0 ~ 3) The index of digital input pin A[pin] :(0 ~ 1) The index of analog input pin Feedback I[pin] V[value] : I[pin] : The index of digital input pin V[value] : {0,1} The value of the digital input signal A[pin] V[value] : A[pin] : The index of analog input pin V[value] : [0 ~ 4095] The value of the analog input signal Example M07 I0 I3 ;read digital pin I0 and I3 >>> I0 V1 >>> I3 V0 M07 A1 ;read analog pin A1 >>> A1 V3946

title: M08 - Read Input Signals Automatically
text: Descriptions M08 is used to read the input signal from the input pins automatically. Usage M08 [I<pin>] M08 [A<pin>] [P<time>] Parameters I[pin] :(0 ~ 3) The index of digital input pin A[pin] :(0 ~ 1) The index of analog input pin P[time] :(ms) The time to read the analog input signal Feedback I[pin] V[value] : I[pin] : The index of digital input pin V[value] : {0,1} The value of the digital input signal A[pin] V[value] : A[pin] : The index of analog input pin V[value] : [0 ~ 4095] The value of the analog input signal Example M08 I0 ;read digital pin I0 automatically M08 A1 P1000 ;read analog pin A1 every 1000ms

title: M09 - Disable Automatic Reading Analog Input Signal
text: Descriptions M09 is used to disable automatic reading the analog input signal. Usage M09 [A<pin>] Parameters A[pin] :(0 ~ 1) The index of analog input pin Example M09 A1 ;disable automatic reading analog pin A1

title: M50 - Enable RJ45
text: Descriptions This command can be used to enable or disable RJ45 port. Usage M50 A<x> Parameter A[x] x = 1 : enable RJ45 x = 0 : disable RJ45 Example M50 A1 ; enable RJ45

title: M51 - Set Ethernet Port
text: Descriptions Set ethernet port number Usage M51 B<x> Parameter B[x] : port number Example M51 B8080 ; set ethernet port

title: M52 - Set MAC Device
text: Descriptions Set MAC address of the robot Usage Address form: A:B:C:D:E:F M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number E[u] : number F[v] : number Example M52 A12 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 >>> MAC add: 12-23-34-45-56-67
syntax: M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v>

title: M53 - Set Ethernet IP
text: Descriptions Set ethernet IP of robot Usage M53 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M53 A192 B168 C1 D1 >>> IP: 192.168.1.1

title: M54 - Set Ethernet DNS
text: Descriptions Set ethernet DNS address Usage M54 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M53 A192 B168 C1 D3 >>> DNS IP: 192.168.1.3

title: M55 - Set Ethernet Gateway
text: Descriptions Set ethernet gateway address Usage M55 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example ; set ethernet gateway address 192.168.3.1 M55 A192 B168 C3 D1

title: M56 - Set Ethernet Subnet
text: Descriptions Set ethernet gateway address Usage M56 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example ; set ethernet subnet address 192.168.3.1 M56 A192 B168 C3 D1

title: M57 - Get Robot IP
text: Descriptions Get the IP of Delta X 2 Plus Robot Usage M57 Example M57 >>> 192.168.2.2

title: M84 - Disable Steppers
text: Descriptions This command can be used to disable steppers. Usage M84

title: M203 - Set Feedrate
text: Descriptions Set movement feedrate. Usage M203 S<value> Parameters S[value] : (mm/s) max feedrate. Example M203 S500 ;Set max feedrate

title: M204 - Set Acceleration
text: Descriptions Set movement acceleration. Usage M204 A<value> Parameters A[value] : (mm/s2) end effector acceleration. Example M204 A5000 ;Set movement acceleration.

title: M205 - Set Begin/End Velocity
text: Descriptions Set segment begin/end velocity. Usage M205 S<value> Parameters S[value] : (mm/s2) end effector begin/end velocity. Example M205 S40 ;Set begin speed at 40 mm/s

title: M206 - Set Axis Offset
text: Descriptions Set home offset for one or all axis. Usage M206 [X<value>] [Y<value>] [Z<value>] Parameters X[value] : (mm) X offset value. Y[value] : (mm) Y offset value. Z[value] : (mm) Z offset value. Example M206 X20 Y-10 Z30 ;Set home offsets

title: M207 - Set Z Safe
text: Descriptions Set the lowest Z level that the robot cannot exceed. Usage M207 [Z<value>] Parameters Z[value] : (mm) Z safe value. Example M207 Z-870 ;Set Z safe value

title: M210 - Set Theta Movement Parameter
text: Descriptions Config theta movement para like speed, accel, jerk, start velocity and end velocity. Usage M210 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters F[value] : (unit/s) speed. A[value] : (unit/s^2) accel. J[value] : (unit/s^3) jerk. S[value] : (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] : (unit/s) end velocity. Example M210 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;set all theta movement para

title: M360 - Select End Effector
text: Descriptions Select the end effector for the robot. You can change the end effector to one of these : Vacuum, gripper, pen, laser, printer or use your custom end effector. Usage M360 E<value> Parameters E[value] 0-Vacuum (default). 1-Gripper 2-Pen 3-Laser 4-Printer 5-Custom Example M360 E2 ;select the end effector is Pen

title: M361 - Set minimum moving distance
text: Descriptions Set the length of minimum moving distance. Usage M361 P<len> Parameters P[len] : (mm) Length in mm. Example M361 P0.1 ;set minium moving distance = 0.1mm

title: M500 - Save Settings
text: Descriptions Save all configurable settings to EEPROM. Usage M500 Example M500 ;Save settings

title: M501 - Restore Settings
text: Descriptions Load all saved settings from EEPROM. Usage M501 Example M501 ;Restore all settings.

title: M502 - Reset Settings
text: Descriptions Reset all configurable settings to their factory defaults. Usage M502 Example M502 ;reset

title: Delta X 2 Plus — G-code reference
text: Gcodes for Delta X 2 G00, G01 - Linear Move Descriptions The G0 and G1 commands add a LINEAR MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage G00 [F<rate>] [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>

title: G0, G1 - Linear Movement
text: Descriptions The G0 and G1 commands add a linear MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Run G28 before the first XYZ move after startup, disabling the motors, or resetting/loading settings. Commands that only set motion parameters or move W/U do not require XYZ homing. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage G1 [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters X[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] :(degrees) Axis W position, within the limits configured by M60 . U[angle] :(degrees) Axis U position, within the limits configured by M61 . F[val] :(mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] :(mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. J[val] :(mm/s³) Jerk, integer from 1 to 10000000. S[val] :(mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] :(mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. Start and end velocities are limited to max(F - 2, 0) . The planner may reduce motion parameters to keep the XYZ step rates within their limits. When this happens, the robot reports Replace F<value> A<value> J<value> S<value> E<value> before Ok , with three decimal places. These are the effective settings for that move; the stored motion settings remain unchanged. Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to X0 Y0 Z-360 G01 X50 ;move to X50, keeping Y0 and Z-360 G01 W90 U45 ;rotate W to 90 degrees and U to 45 degrees G00 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;return to X0 Y0 Z-360 G01 W0 U0 ;return W and U to 0 degrees

title: G2, G3 - Controlled Arc Movement
text: Descriptions On Delta X 3, G2 moves counter-clockwise and G3 moves clockwise , viewed from +Z toward the XY plane. The arc starts at the current XY position and ends at the specified XY position, around the center defined by I and J. Z remains unchanged throughout the arc. Both I and J are required, including when either offset is zero. J specifies the arc center’s Y offset; the previously set jerk remains in use. Run G28 before XYZ motion. Endpoints follow G90 or G91 ; I/J are always offsets from the arc’s starting point. Usage G02 I<offset> J<offset> [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters I[offset] :(mm) An offset from the current X position to use as the arc center. J[offset] :(mm) An offset from the current Y position to use as the arc center. X[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] :(degrees) Axis W position, within the limits configured by M60 . U[angle] :(degrees) Axis U position, within the limits configured by M61 . F[val] :(mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] :(mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. S[val] :(mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] :(mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. These motion settings remain in effect for subsequent moves until changed. Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X50 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the arc's starting point G02 X0 Y50 I-50 J0 ;move 90 degrees counter-clockwise around X0 Y0 G03 X50 Y0 I0 J-50 ;move 90 degrees clockwise back to X50 Y0 Both arcs have a 50 mm radius and a path length of approximately 78.54 mm. Z stays at -360 mm.

title: G4 - Dwell/Delay
text: Descriptions Pause the robot for a period of time. Usage G4 P<value> Parameters P[value] : Required delay in milliseconds, integer from 0 to 4294967295. Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the starting position G04 P500 ;wait 500 ms (0.5 seconds) G01 X50 ;move 50 mm along X after the delay

title: G6 - Theta angle control
text: Descriptions Move the three upper arms to specified Theta angles. Run G28 first. G90 selects absolute joint angles; G91 selects relative angle changes. Motion settings use Cartesian units and remain in effect for subsequent moves until changed. Usage G6 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters X[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. F[val] :(mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] :(mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. J[val] :(mm/s³) Jerk, integer from 1 to 10000000. S[val] :(mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] :(mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute joint angles G6 X0 Y0 Z0 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;move all three upper arms to 0 degrees G6 X10 Y10 Z10 ;move all three upper arms to 10 degrees G6 X0 Y0 Z0 ;return all three upper arms to 0 degrees With the standard X3 geometry, equal joint angles of 0 degrees place the tool at approximately X0 Y0 Z-360.46; equal angles of 10 degrees place it at approximately X0 Y0 Z-382.37 in the base coordinate system.

title: G28 - Homing
text: Descriptions Home the three XYZ motors using their home sensors and move the W and U servos to their configured home positions. W/U do not seek endstops. Homing establishes the XYZ position reference needed for movement and position queries. Usage G28 Example G28 ;home XYZ and move W/U to their configured home angles

title: G90 - Absolute Movement Mode
text: Descriptions In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage G90 Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the starting position G01 X50 ;move to absolute X50 G01 X20 ;move back to absolute X20, a -30 mm change

title: G91 - Relative Movement Mode
text: Descriptions Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage G91 Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the starting position G91 ;use relative positioning G01 X50 ;move +50 mm along X, ending at X50 G01 X-20 Y30 ;move -20 mm in X and +30 mm in Y, ending at X30 Y30 G90 ;restore absolute positioning G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;return to the starting position

title: G93 - Get Current Position
text: Descriptions Get the current XYZ position calculated from the motor steps already emitted. The response uses the robot’s base G-code coordinates, without the working origin set by M206 . Use PositionOffset for coordinates relative to that origin. Run G28 first. If the XYZ reference is unknown, the response is Error:XYZ position is unknown; home with G28. Usage G93 Feedback <xpos>,<ypos>,<zpos> : Coordinates in mm, with two decimal places. <xpos> : Current X position. <ypos> : Current Y position. <zpos> : Current Z position. Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 ;move to the position to query G93 ;read the XYZ position in mm >>> 0.00,0.00,-360.00 The response is an example; the reported position can differ slightly from the target because it is calculated from emitted motor steps.

title: M03, M04 - Output On / Set PWM / Vacuum On
text: Descriptions Turn on a Delta X 3 digital output, set a PWM output, or control the end effector selected by M360 . Usage M03 D<x> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y> M03 S<value> Parameters M03 D[x] or M04 D[x] : Turn on a digital output. x = 0, 1, 2, 3 for the external digital outputs. x = 4 controls the selected end effector. With vacuum mode ( M360 E0 ), it turns the vacuum on. M03 P[x] W[y] : Set a PWM output. x = 0, 1. y = integer from 0 to 255; required. M04 P[x] W[y] : Set a PWM output with a larger value range. x = 0, 1. y = integer from 0 to 65535; required. M03 S[value] or M04 S[value] : Control the selected end effector, with an integer value from 0 to 100. Vacuum ( M360 E0 ): turns the vacuum on. Gripper ( M360 E1 ): positions the gripper within the range configured by M62 ; S0 is fully open and S100 is fully closed. Use separate commands for digital ( D ) and PWM ( P ) outputs. W is used only with PWM outputs. Example M03 D0 ;turn on digital output D0 M05 D0 ;turn off digital output D0 M03 P0 W128 ;set P0 to 128/255, approximately 50.20% PWM M05 P0 ;turn off PWM output P0 M04 P1 W32768 ;set P1 to 32768/65535, approximately 50.00% PWM M05 P1 ;turn off PWM output P1 M360 E0 ;select the vacuum M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum G04 P500 ;keep the vacuum on for 0.5 seconds M05 ;turn off the vacuum M360 E1 ;select the gripper M03 S50 ;move halfway between the configured gripper angle limits G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper
syntax: M03 D<x> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y> M03 S<value>

title: M05 - Output Off / Turn Off PWM / Vacuum Off
text: Descriptions Turn off a Delta X 3 digital output, set a PWM output to zero, or turn off the selected end effector. Usage M05 M05 D<x> M05 P<x> Parameters M05 or M05 D4 : Turn off the end effector selected by M360 . In vacuum mode, turn off the vacuum; in gripper mode, open the gripper. M05 D[x] : turn off digital output pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. M05 P[x] : turn off PWM output pin x = 0, 1. Example M03 D0 ;turn on digital output D0 M05 D0 ;turn off digital output D0 M03 P0 W128 ;enable PWM output P0 M05 P0 ;set P0 PWM to zero M360 E0 ;select the vacuum M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum M05 ;turn off the selected vacuum M360 E1 ;select the gripper M03 S50 ;move the gripper to the middle of its configured range M05 D4 ;open the selected gripper

title: M07 - Read Input Signals.
text: Descriptions Read Digital and Analog input signals. Usage M07 I<x> M07 A<x> Parameters M07 I[x] : Read Digital Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. M07 A[x] : Read Analog Input Pin x = 0, 1. Feedback I[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = [0, 1023] Example M07 I0 I3 ;read digital inputs I0 and I3 >>> I0 V1 >>> I3 V0 M07 A1 ;read analog input A1 on the 0-1023 scale >>> A1 V512 Input values shown are illustrative and depend on the connected signals.

title: M08 - Read Input Signals Automatically.
text: Descriptions Report digital input changes automatically, or report analog input values at a configured interval. Usage M08 I<x> B<y> M08 A<x> C<y> Parameters M08 I[x] B[y] : auto read digital input pins. I[x] : Digital Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. B[y] : Required digital reporting mode. y = 1 : Start the auto-reading digital input signal process. y = 0 : Stop the auto-reading digital input signal process. M08 A[x] C[y] A[x] : Analog Input Pin x = 0, 1. C[y] : Required nonnegative integer interval setting. y > 50 : Enable analog reporting, with an interval of floor(y / 10) milliseconds. For example, C200 sets a 20 ms interval and C5000 sets a 500 ms interval. y <= 50 : Disable analog reporting. Feedback I[x] V[val] : return auto read digital input value x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : return auto read analog input value x = pin number val = [0, 1023] Example M08 I3 B1 ;report each change of digital input I3 M08 A1 C5000 ;report analog input A1 every 500 ms (5000/10) >>> I3 V0 >>> A1 V512 M08 I3 B0 ;stop automatic reports from I3 M08 A1 C0 ;stop automatic reports from A1 Input values shown are illustrative and depend on the connected signals.
syntax: M08 I<x> B<y> M08 A<x> C<y>

title: M9 - Stop Analog Input Auto Feedback
text: Descriptions Turn off auto feedback for an analog input pin. Usage M9 A<n> Parameters A[n] : Analog Input Pin n = 0, 1. Example M08 A1 C5000 ;enable A1 reports at a 500 ms interval G04 P1000 ;wait 1 second M9 A1 ;stop A1 analog reports

title: M43 - Set UART2 / Serial2
text: Descriptions Configure UART2 / Serial2. Use A1 to enable, A0 to disable, and B to set the baudrate. Both parameters are required, including when disabling the port. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied after the reply. Usage M43 A<x> B<y> Parameters A[x] x = 1 : enable UART2 / Serial2. x = 0 : disable UART2 / Serial2. B[y] : Baudrate, integer from 1200 to 3000000. Example M43 A1 B115200 ;enable UART2 / Serial2 at 115200 baud M43 A0 B115200 ;disable UART2 / Serial2 Send these configuration commands through USB so disabling UART2 does not interrupt your control connection.

title: M44 - Set UART3 / Serial3
text: Descriptions Configure UART3 / Serial3. Use A1 to enable, A0 to disable, and B to set the baudrate. Both parameters are required, including when disabling the port. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied after the reply. Usage M44 A<x> B<y> Parameters A[x] x = 1 : enable UART3 / Serial3. x = 0 : disable UART3 / Serial3. B[y] : Baudrate, integer from 1200 to 3000000. Example M44 A1 B115200 ;enable UART3 / Serial3 at 115200 baud M44 A0 B115200 ;disable UART3 / Serial3 Send these configuration commands through USB so disabling UART3 does not interrupt your control connection.

title: M50 - Enable RJ45
text: Descriptions Enable or disable the RJ45 Ethernet port. The setting is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage M50 A<x> Parameter A[x] x = 1 : enable RJ45 x = 0 : disable RJ45 Example M50 A1 ;enable the RJ45 Ethernet port >>> Ok The Ethernet examples use robot IP 192.168.1.100 , DNS/gateway 192.168.1.1 , subnet mask 255.255.255.0 , and TCP port 8844 . Configure the robot through USB; a computer on this subnet can use an unused address such as 192.168.1.10 .

title: M51 - Set Ethernet Port
text: Descriptions Set the Ethernet server port. The setting is saved to EEPROM and the server restarts with the new port. Usage M51 B<x> Parameter B[x] : Port number, integer from 1 to 65535. Example M51 B8844 ;set the Ethernet TCP port to 8844 >>> Ok

title: M52 - Set MAC Device
text: Descriptions Set the robot’s MAC address. All six decimal bytes are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage Address form: A:B:C:D:E:F M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number E[u] : number F[v] : number Example M52 A2 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 ;set MAC bytes to 2-23-34-45-56-67 (decimal) >>> Ok
syntax: M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v>

title: M53 - Set Ethernet IP
text: Descriptions Set the robot’s Ethernet IP address. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage M53 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M53 A192 B168 C1 D100 ;set the robot IP to 192.168.1.100 >>> Ok

title: M54 - Set Ethernet DNS
text: Descriptions Set the Ethernet DNS address. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage M54 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M54 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the DNS server to 192.168.1.1 >>> Ok

title: M55 - Set Ethernet Gateway
text: Descriptions Set the Ethernet gateway address. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The address is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage M55 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M55 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the gateway to 192.168.1.1 >>> Ok

title: M56 - Set Ethernet Subnet
text: Descriptions Set the Ethernet subnet mask. All four decimal octets are required, each from 0 to 255. The mask is saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage M56 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M56 A255 B255 C255 D0 ;use the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet >>> Ok

title: M57 - Get Robot IP
text: Descriptions Get the robot’s configured IP address. Ethernet must be enabled with M50 A1 . Usage M57 Example M53 A192 B168 C1 D100 ;set the robot IP to 192.168.1.100 M50 A1 ;enable Ethernet M57 ;read the configured robot IP >>> IP:192.168.1.100

title: M58 - Get Ethernet Info
text: Descriptions Get the Ethernet enable state, configured IP address, port, MAC address, DNS, gateway, and subnet mask. MAC bytes are reported in decimal. Usage M58 Example M51 B8844 ;set the TCP port M52 A2 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 ;set the MAC address in decimal M53 A192 B168 C1 D100 ;set the robot IP M54 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the DNS server M55 A192 B168 C1 D1 ;set the gateway M56 A255 B255 C255 D0 ;set the subnet mask M50 A1 ;enable Ethernet M58 ;read the Ethernet configuration >>> Ethernet:On;Ip:192.168.1.100;Port:8844;Mac:2-23-34-45-56-67;Dns:192.168.1.1;Gateway:192.168.1.1;Subnet:255.255.255.0

title: M60 - Set Axis W
text: Descriptions Configure the angle limits, home position, and servo pulse widths for axis W. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage M60 [P<x>] [Q<y>] [H<z>] [A<t>] [B<u>] Parameters P[x] : Maximum angle in degrees. Q[y] : Minimum angle in degrees. The limits must satisfy 0 <= Q < P <= 360 . H[z] : Home angle in degrees, within Q <= H <= P . A[t] : Minimum pulse width, integer from 36 to 1056 µs. B[u] : Maximum pulse width, integer from 1892 to 2912 µs. Example M60 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;set W limits to 0-180 degrees, home 90, pulses 500-2500 us G90 ;use absolute positioning G01 W90 ;move W to 90 degrees, corresponding to a 1500 us pulse

title: M61 - Set Axis U
text: Descriptions Configure the angle limits, home position, and servo pulse widths for axis U. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. Usage M61 [P<x>] [Q<y>] [H<z>] [A<t>] [B<u>] Parameters P[x] : Maximum angle in degrees. Q[y] : Minimum angle in degrees. The limits must satisfy 0 <= Q < P <= 360 . H[z] : Home angle in degrees, within Q <= H <= P . A[t] : Minimum pulse width, integer from 36 to 1056 µs. B[u] : Maximum pulse width, integer from 1892 to 2912 µs. Example M61 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;set U limits to 0-180 degrees, home 90, pulses 500-2500 us G90 ;use absolute positioning G01 U90 ;move U to 90 degrees, corresponding to a 1500 us pulse

title: M62 - Set Gripper
text: Descriptions Configure the gripper’s angle limits and home position. Settings are saved to EEPROM and applied automatically. These angles define the range used by M03 S0 through M03 S100 when gripper mode is selected. Usage M62 [P<x>] [Q<y>] [H<z>] Parameters P[x] : Maximum angle in degrees. Q[y] : Minimum angle in degrees. The limits must satisfy 0 <= Q < P <= 360 . H[z] : Home angle in degrees, within Q <= H <= P . Example M62 P100 Q0 H50 ;set gripper limits to 0-100 degrees and home to 50 degrees M360 E1 ;select the gripper M03 S50 ;move to 50% of the 0-100 degree range: 50 degrees G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper to 0 degrees

title: M84 - Disable Steppers
text: Descriptions Disable the stepper motors. The XYZ position reference is cleared; run G28 before the next XYZ move. Usage M84 Example M84 ;disable the stepper motors and clear the XYZ reference

title: M85 - Enable Steppers
text: Descriptions Enable the stepper motors. After M84 , run G28 to restore the XYZ position reference before moving. Usage M85 Example M85 ;enable the stepper motors G28 ;establish the XYZ reference before moving M96 --- ## M98 - Load Sub Program #### Descriptions ... #### Usage M98 --- ## M99 - Stop Sub Program #### Descriptions ... #### Usage M99 --- --> M200 --- -->

title: M203 - Set Jerk
text: Descriptions Set the jerk used for subsequent movements until changed. Usage M203 S<value> Parameters S[value] : Required jerk in mm/s³, integer from 1 to 10000000. Example M203 S550000 ;set jerk to 550000 mm/s^3

title: M204 - Set Max Acceleration
text: Descriptions Set the acceleration used for subsequent movements until changed. Usage M204 A<value> Parameters A[value] : Required acceleration in mm/s², integer from 1 to 50000. Example M204 A15000 ;set acceleration to 15000 mm/s^2

title: M205 - Set Begin/End Velocity
text: Descriptions Set both the start and end velocities for subsequent movements until changed. Usage M205 S<value> Parameters S[value] : Required start/end velocity in mm/s, integer from 0 to 20000. Motion planning limits these velocities to max(F - 2, 0) . Example M205 S50 ;set both start and end velocities to 50 mm/s

title: M206 - Set Axis Offset
text: Descriptions Set the working coordinate origin within the robot’s workspace. Subsequent absolute XYZ targets are relative to this origin. Use PositionOffset to read the current position in the working coordinates. Use M206 X0 Y0 Z0 to return to the base coordinate system. The working origin is not saved by M500 ; resetting or loading settings clears it. Usage M206 [X<value>] [Y<value>] [Z<value>] Parameters X[value] : (mm) Working origin X coordinate in the base coordinate system. Y[value] : (mm) Working origin Y coordinate in the base coordinate system. Z[value] : (mm) Working origin Z coordinate in the base coordinate system. Example G28 ;home the robot G90 ;use absolute positioning M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;use the base coordinate system G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s G01 X20 Y-10 Z-360 ;move to the intended working origin M206 X20 Y-10 Z-360 ;make this point X0 Y0 Z0 in working coordinates G01 X20 Y0 Z0 ;move to base coordinates X40 Y-10 Z-360 G01 X0 Y0 Z0 ;return to the working origin M206 X0 Y0 Z0 ;restore the base coordinate system

title: M207 - Set Z Safe
text: Descriptions Set the lowest Z level that the robot cannot exceed. Usage M207 Z<value> Parameters Z[value] : (mm) Z safe value. Example M207 Z-420 ;set the lowest permitted base Z coordinate to -420 mm

title: M210 - Set Motion Parameters
text: Descriptions Set the Cartesian motion parameters used for subsequent movements. Set these values once; they remain in effect until changed. Usage M210 [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters F[val] :(mm/s) Feed rate, integer from 1 to 20000. A[val] :(mm/s²) Acceleration, integer from 1 to 50000. J[val] :(mm/s³) Jerk, integer from 1 to 10000000. S[val] :(mm/s) Start velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. E[val] :(mm/s) End velocity, integer from 0 to 20000. Start and end velocities are limited to max(F - 2, 0) . Example M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set F=1500 mm/s, A=15000 mm/s^2, J=550000 mm/s^3, S=E=50 mm/s

title: M220 - Read Parameters
text: Descriptions Read robot parameters. Usage M220 [I<n>] Parameters I[n] : Parameter group; defaults to 0. n = 0 : read move parameters. n = 1 : read axis W parameters. n = 2 : read axis U parameters. n = 3 : read gripper parameters. Example M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;configure the motion settings used below M60 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;configure W M61 P180 Q0 H90 A500 B2500 ;configure U M62 P100 Q0 H50 ;configure the gripper M220 I0 ;read motion settings >>> F:1500 A:15000 J:550000 S:50 E:50 M220 I1 ;read W settings >>> WP:180.00 WQ:0.00 WH:90.00 WA:500 WB:2500 M220 I2 ;read U settings >>> UP:180.00 UQ:0.00 UH:90.00 UA:500 UB:2500 M220 I3 ;read gripper settings >>> GP:100.00 GQ:0.00 GH:50.00

title: M360 - Select End Effector
text: Descriptions Select vacuum, gripper, or pen mode for the robot’s end effector. Usage M360 E<value> Parameters E[value] 0-Vacuum (default). 1-Gripper 2-Pen Example M360 E0 ;select vacuum mode M03 D4 ;turn on the vacuum G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;turn off the vacuum M360 E1 ;select gripper mode M03 S50 ;move to the middle of the configured gripper range G04 P500 ;wait 0.5 seconds M05 ;open the gripper M360 E2 ;select pen mode

title: M361 - Set minimum movement
text: Descriptions Set the minimum movement distance. The default and smallest allowed value are 0.1 mm. Usage M361 P<len> Parameters P[len] : (mm) Minimum movement distance, from 0.1 to 1000000 mm. Example M361 P0.1 ;set the minimum movement distance to 0.1 mm

title: M500 - Save Settings
text: Descriptions Save persistent settings to EEPROM, including motion parameters, axis/gripper calibration, robot geometry, and communication settings. The working origin set by M206 is not saved. Usage M500 Example M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set the motion parameters M500 ;save the current persistent settings to EEPROM >>> Ok

title: M501 - Reset Settings
text: Descriptions Reset settings to their defaults and save them to EEPROM. This also clears the working origin and XYZ position reference. Run G28 before the next XYZ move. Usage M501 Example M501 ;reset settings to defaults and save them to EEPROM G28 ;home again before XYZ movement

title: M502 - Load Settings
text: Descriptions Load saved settings from EEPROM. This also clears the working origin and XYZ position reference. Run G28 before the next XYZ move. Usage M502 Example M210 F1500 A15000 J550000 S50 E50 ;set the motion parameters M500 ;save these settings to EEPROM M210 F1000 ;temporarily change the feed rate to 1000 mm/s M502 ;reload the saved settings, restoring F1500 M220 I0 ;verify the restored motion parameters >>> F:1500 A:15000 J:550000 S:50 E:50 G28 ;home again before XYZ movement

Run G28 before the first XYZ move after startup, disabling the motors, or resetting/loading settings. Commands that only set motion parameters or move W/U do not require XYZ homing. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subs
