title: G0, G1 - Linear Movement
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions The G0 and G1 commands add a linear MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage G1 [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters X[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] :(unit) Axis 4 position. U[angle] :(unit) Axis 5 position. V[angle] :(unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] :(mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] :(mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. J[val] :(mm/s3) Jerk of the motion. S[val] :(mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] :(mm/s) Finish velocity. For W/U/V, a unit is a degree for a rotary axis or a millimeter for a linear axis, according to its steps-per-unit configuration. Example G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S100 E100 ; Set the feed rate to 1500 mm/s, acceleration to 15000 mm/s², jerk to 550000 mm/s³, start velocity to 100 mm/s, and end velocity to 100 mm/s. G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 ; Move to the absolute position (X0, Y0, Z-750). G01 X50 ; Move to X = 50 mm. G01 W90 ; Rotate to 90° on the 4-axis

title: G2, G3 - Controlled Arc Movement
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Add an arc move in the XY plane, keeping Z unchanged. I and J locate the center relative to the arc’s starting point. Use G90 absolute positioning for arc commands. In this XS V4 implementation, G2 moves counter-clockwise and G3 moves clockwise , viewed from positive Z toward the XY plane. Use the directions shown here when preparing commands for XS V4. Usage G02 I<offset> J<offset> [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Use G03 for the opposite direction. Always include both I and J , even when one offset is zero. Here, J is the Y center offset; the previously configured jerk remains in use. Parameters I[offset] :(mm) Required X offset from the starting point to the arc center. J[offset] :(mm) Required Y offset from the starting point to the arc center. X[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] , U[angle] , V[angle] :(unit) Axis 4, 5, and 6 positions, using the configured units for each axis. F[val] :(mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] :(mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. S[val] :(mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] :(mm/s) Finish velocity. Example G28 ; Home all axes. G90 ; Use absolute positioning. G01 X50 Y20 Z-750 F200 ; Move to the arc start at (X50, Y20, Z-750). G02 X20 Y50 I-30 J0 F200 ; Counter-clockwise 90° arc around (X20, Y20), radius 30 mm. G03 X50 Y20 I0 J-30 F200 ; Clockwise 90° arc back to (X50, Y20). Both arcs keep Z at -750 mm. The X/Y endpoints are absolute positions; I/J are offsets from each arc’s starting point to the center at (X20, Y20). Keep the center’s X coordinate nonzero for this implementation.

title: G4 - Dwell/Delay
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Pause the robot for a period of time. Usage G4 P<value> Parameters P[value] : delay in milliseconds. Example G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 F1500 A15000 J550000 S100 E100 G4 P500 ;delay 500ms G01 X50

title: G6 - Theta angle control
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Specify the target Theta 1, 2, and 3 angles instead of Cartesian endpoint coordinates. Axis 6 is selected with R in this command. Usage G6 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] [W<pos>] [U<pos>] [R<pos>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters X[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. W[pos] :(unit) Axis 4 position. U[pos] :(unit) Axis 5 position. R[pos] :(unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] :(mm/s) Cartesian feed rate. A[val] :(mm/s²) Cartesian acceleration. J[val] :(mm/s³) Cartesian jerk. S[val] :(mm/s) Start velocity. E[val] :(mm/s) End velocity. W/U/R use the configured units for their axes: degrees for rotary axes or millimeters for linear axes. Omitted F/A/J/S/E values keep their current motion settings, which also apply to subsequent moves until changed. Example G90 ; Use absolute positioning. G6 X20 Y0 Z0 F200 ; Move to Theta 1 = 20°, Theta 2 = 0°, Theta 3 = 0° at 200 mm/s.

title: G28 - Homing
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Auto-home all axes, moving them towards their endstops until triggered. Usage G28

title: G90 - Absolute Movement Mode
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage G90

title: G91 - Relative Movement Mode
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage G91

title: G93 - Get Current Position
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Read the Cartesian position stored by the controller. The response is always sent through USB, including when the command arrives on another port. Usage G93 Feedback The response contains <xpos>,<ypos>,<zpos> in millimeters, with two decimal places. Auxiliary-axis positions are omitted. The reported Z includes the robot’s configured vertical reference offset. For example, with a 188.5 mm offset and no user coordinate offset, a G-code position of Z-750 is reported as Z-561.50. Use M100 for automatic position reports in the G-code coordinate frame. Example G93 ; Read the Cartesian position through USB. Example USB response at X0 Y0 Z-750, with a 188.5 mm vertical reference offset: 0.00,0.00,-561.50

title: M03, M04 - Set Digital Output / PWM
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set digital output states or PWM values. M03 uses 8-bit PWM values; M04 uses 16-bit PWM values. Both commands can set digital outputs with D . Usage M03 D<x> W<state> M04 D<x> W<state> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y> Parameters M03 D[x] W[state] , M04 D[x] W[state] : set digital outputs. x = 0, 1, 2, … 15. state = 1 : turn on; state = 0 : turn off. M03 P[x] W[y] : turn on PWM pins x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. y = [0, 255] M04 P[x] W[y] : turn on PWM pins but with larger pwm range. x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. y = [0, 65535]. Always include W , including for digital outputs. Several outputs can be selected on one line, such as M03 D0 D1 W1 . Example G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. G01 Z-700
syntax: M03 D<x> W<state> M04 D<x> W<state> M03 P<x> W<y> M04 P<x> W<y>

title: M05 - Turn Off Digital Output / PWM
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Turn off selected digital outputs or set selected PWM outputs to zero. Usage M05 D<x> M05 P<x> Parameters M05 D[x] : turn off digital output pin x = 0, 1, 2, … 15. M05 P[x] : turn off PWM output pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15. Several outputs can be selected on one line. Specify at least one D or P output; a bare M05 does not select all outputs. Example G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. G01 Z-780 G04 P300 G01 Z-750 G01 X50 Y50 M05 D0 ; Turn off digital output D0.

title: M07 - Read Input Signals.
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Read selected digital input states or raw analog input values. Several channels can be selected on one line. Usage M07 I<x> M07 A<x> Parameters M07 I[x] : Read Digital Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. M07 A[x] : Read Analog Input Pin x = 0, 1, 2, 3. Feedback I[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : x = pin number val = [0, 4095] Example M07 I0 I3 A2 ; Read digital inputs I0 and I3, and analog input A2. Example responses; values depend on the connected signals: I0 V1 I3 V0 A2 V3946

title: M08 - Read Input Signals Automatically.
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure automatic input reports. Digital inputs report state changes; analog inputs report sampled values at the requested interval. Usage M08 I<pin> [B<enable>] [P<port>] M08 A<pin> [C<period_us>] [P<port>] Parameters Parameter Values and function I<pin> Digital input index: 0 – 7 . Several inputs can be selected on one line. B<enable> Digital reports: 1 enables reporting; 0 disables it. Default: 1 when omitted. A<pin> Analog input index: 0 – 3 . Several channels can be selected on one line. C<period_us> Requested analog report interval in microseconds. Default: 500000 (500 ms) when omitted. The I/O board determines the supported minimum interval and the value used to disable analog reports. P<port> Report destination: 0 = USB, 1 = RS232, 3 = TTL, 4 = Ethernet (RJ45). The startup report destination is USB. Open the selected port before requesting reports on it. RS485 ( P2 ) is rejected with Unknown: This function cannot be used on RS485! . Feedback I[x] V[val] : return auto read digital input value x = pin number val = {0,1} A[x] V[val] : return auto read analog input value x = pin number val = [0, 4095] Example M08 I3 B1 P0 ; Report changes on input I3 through USB. M08 A2 C500000 P0 ; Request analog input A2 reports every 500 ms through USB. Example automatic reports; values depend on the connected signals: I3 V0 A2 V2478 To stop automatic reports for digital input I3: M08 I3 B0

title: M40 - Open RS232 port.
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Enable/Disable RS232 port and set baudrate. Usage M40 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters M40 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close RS232 port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close port B[y] : baud rate. Example M40 A1 B115200 ;Open RS232 port and set baudrate at 115200

title: M41 - Open RS485 port
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Enable/Disable RS485 port and set baudrate. Usage M41 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters M41 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close RS485 port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close Port B[y] : baud rate. Note: When control Delta X S via RS485, after each time sending a G-code command to the robot, you must wait for a response from the robot before sending the next G-code command. Otherwise, the communication will not be successful. Example M41 A1 B115200 ;Open RS485 port and set baudrate at 115200

title: M42 - Open TTL port.
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Enable/Disable TTL port and set baudrate. Usage M42 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters M42 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close TTL port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close Port B[y] : baud rate. Example M42 A1 B115200 ;Open TTL port and set baudrate at 115200

title: M49 - Get Ports Config
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Read the enabled state and configured baud rate of USB, RS232, RS485, and TTL, followed by the Ethernet enabled state and server port number. Usage M49 Example M49 Example response; values depend on the current configuration: USB:1 BAUD:115200 RS232:0 BAUD:115200 RS485:1 BAUD:115200 TTL:1 BAUD:115200 RJ45:1 Port:8080 Ok

title: M50 - Enable RJ45
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions This command can be used to enable or disable RJ45 port. Usage M50 A<x> Parameter A[x] x = 1 : enable RJ45 x = 0 : disable RJ45 Example M50 A1 ; enable RJ45

title: M51 - Set Ethernet Port
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set ethernet port number Usage M51 B<x> Parameter B[x] : port number Example M51 B8080 ; set ethernet port

title: M52 - Set MAC Device
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set the robot’s MAC address and save it to EEPROM. Usage Provide all six bytes in A:B:C:D:E:F order, using decimal integers from 0 to 255. M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number E[u] : number F[v] : number Example M52 A2 B23 C34 D45 E56 F67 ; Set MAC address 02:17:22:2D:38:43 (hex). Response: Ok
syntax: M52 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> E<u> F<v>

title: M53 - Set Ethernet IP
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set the robot’s Ethernet IP address for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four address octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage M53 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M53 A192 B168 C1 D5 ; Set the robot IP address to 192.168.1.5. Response: Ok

title: M54 - Set Ethernet DNS
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set the Ethernet DNS server address for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four address octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage M54 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M54 A192 B168 C1 D1 ; Set the DNS server to 192.168.1.1. Response: Ok

title: M55 - Set Ethernet Gateway
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set the Ethernet gateway address for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four address octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage M55 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example ; set ethernet gateway address 192.168.1.1 M55 A192 B168 C1 D1

title: M56 - Set Ethernet Subnet
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set the Ethernet subnet mask for the current session. A/B/C/D are the four mask octets, each a decimal integer from 0 to 255; all four are required. Usage M56 A<x> B<y> C<z> D<t> Parameter A[x] : number B[y] : number C[z] : number D[t] : number Example M56 A255 B255 C255 D0 ; Set the subnet mask to 255.255.255.0.

title: M57 - Get Robot IP
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Read the active Ethernet IP address and server port number. Enable Ethernet with M50 A1 and connect the Ethernet cable before sending this command. The response has the form IP:<address>:<port> . If Ethernet is unavailable, the response indicates that RJ45 is disabled, the Ethernet hardware is missing, or the cable is disconnected. Usage M57 Example M57 Example response with IP address 192.168.1.5 and server port 8080: IP:192.168.1.5:8080

title: M60 - Set Axis 4 Parameters
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure axis 4. Units are degrees for a rotary axis or millimeters for a linear axis, according to the steps-per-unit setting. Use M500 to store the configuration in EEPROM. Usage M60 [D<val>] [E<val>] [I<val>] [S<val>] [R<val>] [U<val>] [P<val>] [Q<val>] [H<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [F<val>] Parameter D[val] : enable axis 4 val = 1 : enable axis 4 val = 0 : disable axis 4 E[val] : enable endstop val = 1 : enable axis 4 endstop val = 0 : disable axis 4 endstop I[val] : set invert endstop logic level val = 1 : axis 4 endstop invert val = 0 : axis 4 endstop non-invert S[val] : (unit/s) homing speed R[val] : (unit) distance to back away from the endstop during homing U[val] : (step/unit) set step/unit parameter P[val] : (unit) set max position Q[val] : (unit) set min position H[val] : (unit) set home position A[val] : (unit/s²) maximum acceleration J[val] : (unit/s³) maximum jerk F[val] : (unit/s) maximum velocity Example M60 D1 E1 I0 S30 R20 U8.333330 P180 Q-179 H2 A150000 J5000000 F2000

title: M61 - Set Axis 5 Parameters
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure axis 5. Units are degrees for a rotary axis or millimeters for a linear axis, according to the steps-per-unit setting. Use M500 to store the configuration in EEPROM. Usage M61 [D<val>] [E<val>] [I<val>] [S<val>] [R<val>] [U<val>] [P<val>] [Q<val>] [H<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [F<val>] Parameter D[val] : enable axis 5 val = 1 : enable val = 0 : disable E[val] : enable endstop val = 1 : enable axis 5 endstop val = 0 : disable axis 5 endstop I[val] : set invert endstop logic level val = 1 : axis 5 endstop invert val = 0 : axis 5 endstop non-invert S[val] : (unit/s) homing speed R[val] : (unit) distance to back away from the endstop during homing U[val] : (step/unit) set step/unit parameter P[val] : (unit) set max position Q[val] : (unit) set min position H[val] : (unit) set home position A[val] : (unit/s²) maximum acceleration J[val] : (unit/s³) maximum jerk F[val] : (unit/s) maximum velocity Example M61 D1 E1 I0 S30 R20 U8.888888 P95 Q-100 H2 A20000 J2000000 F2000

title: M62 - Set Axis 6 Parameters
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure axis 6. Units are degrees for a rotary axis or millimeters for a linear axis, according to the steps-per-unit setting. Use M500 to store the configuration in EEPROM. Usage M62 [D<val>] [E<val>] [I<val>] [S<val>] [R<val>] [U<val>] [P<val>] [Q<val>] [H<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [F<val>] Parameter D[val] : enable axis 6 val = 1 : enable val = 0 : disable E[val] : enable endstop val = 1 : enable axis 6 endstop val = 0 : disable axis 6 endstop I[val] : set invert endstop logic level val = 1 : axis 6 endstop invert val = 0 : axis 6 endstop non-invert S[val] : (unit/s) homing speed R[val] : (unit) distance to back away from the endstop during homing U[val] : (step/unit) set step/unit parameter P[val] : (unit) set max position Q[val] : (unit) set min position H[val] : (unit) set home position A[val] : (unit/s²) maximum acceleration J[val] : (unit/s³) maximum jerk F[val] : (unit/s) maximum velocity Example M62 D1 E1 I0 S30 R20 U8.333333 P20 Q-100 H1 A15000 J500000 F4000

title: M84 - Disable Steppers
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions This command can be used to disable steppers. Usage M84

title: M100 - Set Auto Feedback Position
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure automatic position reports and their destination port. Usage M100 [A<mode>] [B<time>] [C<port>] Parameter A[mode] : reporting mode. 0 : disable reports. 1 : report periodically during movement. 2 : report periodically during movement and while idle. B[time] : report interval in milliseconds. Use at least 10 ; a value below 10 disables reporting. C[port] : destination port. 0 : USB. 1 : RS232. 3 : TTL. 4 : Ethernet (RJ45). RS485 ( C2 ) is rejected with Unknown: This function cannot be used on RS485! . Open the selected port before requesting reports on it. Each report starts with Position: , followed by X/Y/Z and the positions of enabled W/U/V axes in that order. Values have two decimal places. Example M100 A1 B200 C0 ; Report position on USB every 200 ms during movement. Example report with auxiliary axes disabled: Position:0.00,0.00,-750.00 To report every 200 ms even while idle: M100 A2 B200 C0 To stop automatic position reports: M100 A0 C0 M200 --- -->

title: M203 - Set Jerk
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set movement jerk of end effector. Usage M203 J<value> Parameters J[value] : (mm/s³) required jerk value. Omitting J returns Unknown:Gcode wrong! . Example M203 J1200000 ;set jerk = 1.200.000 mm/s^3

title: M204 - Set Max Acceleration
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set movement acceleration. Usage M204 A<value> Parameters A[value] : (mm/s²) required end-effector acceleration. Omitting A returns Unknown:Gcode wrong! . Example M204 A15000 ;set accel = 15000 mm/s^2

title: M205 - Set Begin/End Velocity
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set both the start and end velocity of a movement segment to the same value. Usage M205 S<value> Parameters S[value] : (mm/s) required start and end velocity. Omitting S returns Unknown:Gcode wrong! . Example M205 S40 ; Set both start and end velocity to 40 mm/s.

title: M206 - Set Axis Offset
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set the origin offset used by absolute movement commands. The specified origin must be within the robot’s configured workspace and axis limits. Usage M206 [X<value>] [Y<value>] [Z<value>] [W<value>] [U<value>] [V<value>] Parameters X[value] : (mm) X offset value. Y[value] : (mm) Y offset value. Z[value] : (mm) Z offset value. W[value] : (unit) W offset value, in the configured axis units. U[value] : (unit) U offset value, in the configured axis units. V[value] : (unit) V offset value, in the configured axis units. Example M206 X20 Y-10 Z-750 W0 U0 ; Set the XYZ origin to (20, -10, -750) and W/U offsets to zero.

title: M207 - Set Z Safe
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set the lowest permitted Z coordinate and save it to EEPROM. A value below the workspace limit is rejected. A value above the home Z coordinate disables the additional Z limit. Usage M207 Z<value> Parameters Z[value] : (mm) lowest permitted Z coordinate. Always specify Z; sending M207 without it disables the limit. Example M207 Z-870 ; Set the lowest permitted Z coordinate to -870 mm. The example requires -870 mm to be within the configured workspace and at or below the home Z coordinate.

title: M210 - Set Theta Movement Parameter
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure Cartesian movement speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity for the Theta group. Set these motion parameters once; they apply to subsequent moves for this group until changed. Omitted motion parameters keep their current values. Usage M210 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters F[value] : (mm/s) speed. A[value] : (mm/s²) acceleration. J[value] : (mm/s³) jerk. S[value] : (mm/s) start velocity. E[value] : (mm/s) end velocity. Example M210 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;set all theta movement para

title: M211 - Set Axis 4 Movement Parameter
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure axis 4 speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity. Enable the axis with M60 first and keep the requested values within its configured limits. Set these motion parameters once; they apply to subsequent moves for this group until changed. Omitted motion parameters keep their current values. Usage M211 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters F[value] : (unit/s) axis 4 speed. A[value] : (unit/s^2) axis 4 accel. J[value] : (unit/s^3) axis 4 jerk. S[value] : (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] : (unit/s) end velocity. Example M211 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;config axis 4 move para

title: M212 - Set Axis 5 Movement Parameter
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure axis 5 speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity. Enable the axis with M61 first and keep the requested values within its configured limits. Set these motion parameters once; they apply to subsequent moves for this group until changed. Omitted motion parameters keep their current values. Usage M212 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters F[value] : (unit/s) axis 5 speed. A[value] : (unit/s^2) axis 5 accel. J[value] : (unit/s^3) axis 5 jerk. S[value] : (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] : (unit/s) end velocity. Example M212 F2000 A4000 J800000 S30 E30 ;config axis 5 move para

title: M213 - Set Axis 6 Movement Parameter
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Axis 6 movement parameters: speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity. Usage M213 [F<value>] [A<value>] [J<value>] [S<value>] [E<value>] Parameters F[value] : (unit/s) speed. A[value] : (unit/s^2) acceleration. J[value] : (unit/s^3) jerk. S[value] : (unit/s) start velocity. E[value] : (unit/s) end velocity. Example M213 F2000 A4000 J500000 S30 E30 ; Set movement speed, acceleration, jerk, start velocity, and end velocity.

title: M220 - Get Current Axis Parameter
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Read the current movement parameters of one axis group. Omitting I selects the Theta group ( I0 ). Usage M220 [I<val>] Parameter I[val] : axis index val = 0 : get theta parameter val = 1 : get axis 4 parameter val = 2 : get axis 5 parameter val = 3 : get axis 6 parameter The Theta group uses response labels F, A, J, S, and E. Axis 4 uses WF, WA, WJ, WS, and WE; axes 5 and 6 use the corresponding U and V prefixes. The selected auxiliary axis must be enabled. Example M220 I1 ; Read axis 4 movement parameters. Example response for an enabled W axis configured with these values: WF:2000.00 WA:4000.00 WJ:800000.00 WS:30.00 WE:30.00

title: M500 - Save Settings
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Save the current motion parameters and supported configuration settings to EEPROM. IP, DNS, gateway, and subnet values set by M53–M56 are session settings and are not stored by M500 on XS V4. Usage M500 Example M500 ;Save settings

title: M501 - Reset Settings
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Reset settings to the firmware defaults and immediately save them to EEPROM. This overwrites the previously saved settings; an additional M500 is unnecessary. Usage M501 Example M501 ; Reset settings to firmware defaults and save them to EEPROM.

title: M502 - Load Settings
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Reload the saved motion parameters and supported configuration settings from EEPROM. Usage M502 Example M502 ; Reload the settings saved in EEPROM.

title: M600 - Enable Emergency Stop Button
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Enable emergency-stop monitoring using the standard XS V4 E-stop inputs I8 and I9 , and save the selection to EEPROM. Usage M600 A8 B9 Example M600 A8 B9 ; Enable emergency-stop monitoring on the standard inputs I8 and I9.

title: M601 - Disable Emergency Stop Button
page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Disable E_STOP button. Usage M601 Example M601 ;disable E_STOP button

page: Delta X S V4 — G-code reference

Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. title: G0, G1 - Linear Movement
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions The G0 and G1 commands add a linear MOVE to the queue to be performed after all previous moves are completed. Set F (feed rate), A (acceleration), J (jerk), S (start velocity), and E (end velocity) once. Subsequent movement commands use these settings until changed; motion parameters omitted from a command keep their current settings. Usage G1 [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [Z<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters X[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. Z[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Z-axis. W[angle] :(unit) Axis 4 position. U[angle] :(unit) Axis 5 position. V[angle] :(unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] :(mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] :(mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. J[val] :(mm/s3) Jerk of the motion. S[val] :(mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] :(mm/s) Finish velocity. For W/U/V, a unit is a degree for a rotary axis or a millimeter for a linear axis, according to its steps-per-unit configuration. Example G01 F1500 A15000 J550000 S100 E100 ; Set the feed rate to 1500 mm/s, acceleration to 15000 mm/s², jerk to 550000 mm/s³, start velocity to 100 mm/s, and end velocity to 100 mm/s. G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 ; Move to the absolute position (X0, Y0, Z-750). G01 X50 ; Move to X = 50 mm. G01 W90 ; Rotate to 90° on the 4-axis

title: G2, G3 - Controlled Arc Movement
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions G2 adds a clockwise arc move to the planner; G3 adds a counter-clockwise arc. The arc runs in the XY plane from the current position to the specified X/Y endpoint, keeping Z unchanged. I and J locate the center relative to the arc’s starting point. Usage G02 I<offset> J<offset> [X<pos>] [Y<pos>] [W<angle>] [U<angle>] [V<angle>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Use G03 for a counter-clockwise arc. Always include both I and J , even when one offset is zero. In these commands, J is the Y center offset; the previously configured jerk remains in use. Parameters I[offset] :(mm) Required X offset from the starting point to the arc center. J[offset] :(mm) Required Y offset from the starting point to the arc center. X[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the X-axis. Y[pos] :(mm) A coordinate on the Y-axis. W[angle] , U[angle] , V[angle] :(unit) Axis 4, 5, and 6 positions, using the configured units for each axis. F[val] :(mm/s) The maximum movement rate of the move between the start and endpoint. The feedrate set here applies to subsequent moves that omit this parameter. A[val] :(mm/s2) Acceleration of the motion. S[val] :(mm/s) Begin velocity. E[val] :(mm/s) Finish velocity. Example G28 ; Home all axes. G90 ; Use absolute positioning. G01 X50 Y0 Z-750 F200 ; Move to the arc start at (X50, Y0, Z-750). G02 X0 Y-50 I-50 J0 F200 ; Clockwise 90° arc around (X0, Y0), radius 50 mm. G03 X50 Y0 I0 J50 F200 ; Counter-clockwise 90° arc back to (X50, Y0). Both arcs keep Z at -750 mm. The X/Y endpoints are absolute positions; I/J are offsets from each arc’s starting point to the center at (X0, Y0).

title: G4 - Dwell/Delay
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Pause the robot for a period of time. Usage G4 P<value> Parameters P[value] : delay in milliseconds. Example G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 F1500 A15000 J550000 S100 E100 G4 P500 ;delay 500ms G01 X50

title: G6 - Theta angle control
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Specify the target Theta 1, 2, and 3 angles instead of Cartesian endpoint coordinates. Axis 6 is selected with R in this command. Usage G6 [X<angle>] [Y<angle>] [Z<angle>] [W<pos>] [U<pos>] [R<pos>] [F<val>] [A<val>] [J<val>] [S<val>] [E<val>] Parameters X[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 1 angle. Y[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 2 angle. Z[angle] :(degree) The value of the Theta 3 angle. W[pos] :(unit) Axis 4 position. U[pos] :(unit) Axis 5 position. R[pos] :(unit) Axis 6 position. F[val] :(mm/s) Cartesian feed rate. A[val] :(mm/s²) Cartesian acceleration. J[val] :(mm/s³) Cartesian jerk. S[val] :(mm/s) Start velocity. E[val] :(mm/s) End velocity. W/U/R use the configured units for their axes: degrees for rotary axes or millimeters for linear axes. Omitted F/A/J/S/E values keep their current motion settings, which also apply to subsequent moves until changed. Example G90 ; Use absolute positioning. G6 X20 Y0 Z0 F200 ; Move to Theta 1 = 20°, Theta 2 = 0°, Theta 3 = 0° at 200 mm/s.

title: G28 - Homing
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Auto-home all axes, moving them towards their endstops until triggered. Usage G28

title: G90 - Absolute Movement Mode
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions In absolute mode, all coordinates given in G-code are interpreted as positions in the logical coordinate space. Usage G90

title: G91 - Relative Movement Mode
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set relative position mode. In this mode, all coordinates are interpreted as relative to the last position. Usage G91

title: G93 - Get Current Position
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Read the current Cartesian position and the positions of enabled auxiliary axes. Usage G93 Feedback The response begins with <xpos>,<ypos>,<zpos> in millimeters. Positions of enabled W, U, and V axes follow in that order, using each axis’s configured units. Disabled axes are omitted. Values have two decimal places. Positive values have no leading + sign or zero padding. Example G93 ; Read the current position. Example response with auxiliary axes disabled: 0.00,0.00,-750.00 Example response with only axis W enabled, at 90°: 0.00,0.00,-750.00,90.00

title: M03, M04 - Set Digital Output / PWM
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Set digital output states or PWM values. M03 uses 8-bit PWM values; M04 uses 16-bit PWM values. Both commands can set digital outputs with D . Usage M03 D<pin> W<state> M04 D<pin> W<state> M03 P<pin> W<value> M04 P<pin> W<value> Parameters Parameter Values and function D<pin> Digital output index: 0 – 7 . Use W1 to turn it on or W0 to turn it off. P<pin> PWM output index: 0 – 7 . W<value> with M03 P... 8-bit PWM value: 0 – 255 . W<value> with M04 P... 16-bit PWM value: 0 – 65535 . Always include W , including for digital outputs. Several outputs can be selected on one line, such as M03 D0 D1 W1 . D and P select digital or PWM control of the output with that index. Example M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. M03 D1 D2 W1 ; Turn on digital outputs D1 and D2. M03 P3 W128 ; Set PWM output P3 to 128 on the 8-bit scale (0–255). M04 P4 W32768 ; Set PWM output P4 to 32768 on the 16-bit scale (0–65535). M03 D0 W0 ; Turn off digital output D0. Each command returns Ok .
syntax: M03 D<pin> W<state> M04 D<pin> W<state> M03 P<pin> W<value> M04 P<pin> W<value>

title: M05 - Turn Off Digital Output / PWM
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Turn off selected digital outputs or set selected PWM outputs to zero. Usage M05 D<pin> M05 P<pin> Parameters Parameter Values and function D<pin> Digital output index: 0 – 7 . Set the selected output to OFF. P<pin> PWM output index: 0 – 7 . Set the selected PWM value to zero. Several outputs can be selected on one line. Specify at least one D or P output; a bare M05 does not select all outputs. Example M03 D0 W1 ; Turn on digital output D0. M05 D0 ; Turn off digital output D0. M03 P1 W128 ; Set PWM output P1 to 128 on the 8-bit scale. M05 P1 ; Set PWM output P1 to zero. M05 D2 D3 P4 ; Turn off D2 and D3, and set PWM output P4 to zero. Each command returns Ok .

title: M07 - Read Input Signals.
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Read the current state of selected digital inputs or the raw ADC values of selected analog inputs. Several digital and analog channels can be requested on one line. Usage M07 I<pin> M07 A<pin> M07 I<digital_pin> A<analog_pin> Parameters Parameter Values and function I<pin> Digital input index: 0 – 5 . A<pin> Analog input index: 0 or 1 . Feedback Response Meaning I<pin> V<value> Digital input state: 0 or 1 . A<pin> V<value> Raw 12-bit ADC value: 0 – 4095 . One response is returned per selected input when the I/O board replies. Specify at least one input from the ranges above. Example M07 I0 I3 A1 ; Read digital inputs I0 and I3, and analog input A1. Example responses; values depend on the connected signals: I0 V1 I3 V0 A1 V2478
syntax: M07 I<pin> M07 A<pin> M07 I<digital_pin> A<analog_pin>

title: M08 - Read Input Signals Automatically.
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure automatic input reports. Digital inputs report state changes; analog inputs report sampled values at the requested interval. Usage M08 I<pin> [B<enable>] [P<port>] M08 A<pin> [C<period_us>] [P<port>] Parameters Parameter Values and function I<pin> Digital input index: 0 – 5 . Several inputs can be selected on one line. B<enable> Digital reports: 1 enables reporting; 0 disables it. Default: 1 when omitted. A<pin> Analog input index: 0 or 1 . Both channels can be selected on one line. C<period_us> Requested analog report period in microseconds. Default: 500000 (500 ms) when omitted. The I/O-board firmware determines the supported minimum period and the value used to disable analog reports. P<port> Report destination: 0 = USB0, 1 = RS232, 2 = RS485, 3 = USB1. The startup report destination is USB0. Open the selected serial port before requesting reports on it. RS485 ( P2 ) requires full-duplex mode; half-duplex mode returns Unknown: This function cannot be used on RS485! . Ethernet ( P4 ) is not accepted by M08 . Digital inputs assigned to an enabled emergency stop are used for E-stop monitoring instead of ordinary automatic digital reports. Feedback Each configuration command returns Ok . Reports then arrive as: Response Meaning I<pin> V<value> Digital input state: 0 or 1 . A<pin> V<value> Raw 12-bit ADC value: 0 – 4095 . Example M08 I3 B1 P0 ; Report changes on digital input I3 through USB0. M08 A1 C500000 P0 ; Request analog input A1 reports every 500 ms through USB0. Example automatic reports; values depend on the connected signals: I3 V0 A1 V2478 To stop automatic reports for digital input I3: M08 I3 B0 ; Disable automatic reports for digital input I3.

title: M40 - Open RS232 port.
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Enable/Disable RS232 port and set baudrate. Usage M40 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters M40 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close RS232 port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close port B[y] : baud rate. Example M40 A1 B115200 ;Open RS232 port and set baudrate at 115200

title: M41 - Open RS485 port
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Enable/Disable RS485 port and set baudrate. Usage M41 A<x> [B<y>] Parameters M41 A[x] B[y] A[x] : Open/Close RS485 port x = 1 : Open Port x = 0 : Close Port B[y] : baud rate. Note: When control Delta X S via RS485, after each time sending a G-code command to the robot, you must wait for a response from the robot before sending the next G-code command. Otherwise, the communication will not be successful. Example M41 A1 B115200 ;Open RS485 port and set baudrate at 115200

title: M42 - Open USB1 port.
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference

title: M100 - Set Auto Feedback Position
page: Delta X S V5 — G-code reference
text: Descriptions Configure automatic position reports and their destination port. Usage M100 [A<mode>] [B<time>] [C<port>] Parameter A[mode] : reporting mode. 0 : disable reports. 1 : report during movement, plus the final position when movement completes. 2 : report periodically during movement and while idle. B[time] : report interval in milliseconds. Use at least 10 ; a value below 10 disables reporting. C[port] : destination port. 0 : USB0. 1 : RS232. 3 : USB1. 4 : Ethernet (RJ45). title: Identify Delta Robot Command
text: To check if a COM port is connected to a Delta Robot, send the command IsDelta . If connected, it replies with YesDelta . The baudrate should be 115200. IsDelta >>> YesDelta Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .

title: Disconnect COM Port Command
text: Send Disconnect when ending a control session. Disconnect On Delta X 3 , this updates the connection state and indicator. Close the COM port in your host application to release the serial connection. Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .

title: Get Current Position Command
text: To retrieve the robot’s current end-effector position, use the Position command. The response format depends on the model. Delta X 1 / Delta X 2 / Delta X S Position >>> X30.4 Y90 Z-800 W50 U90 Delta X 3 returns X,Y,Z in mm, with two decimal places, calculated from emitted motor steps. The coordinates use the robot’s base frame, without the working origin set by M206 ; W/U are not included. G93 returns the same position. Position >>> 31.00,43.00,-291.00 Run G28 before using Position , PositionOffset , or Angle on X3. If the XYZ reference is unknown, these commands return Error:XYZ position is unknown; home with G28. Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .
syntax: Position >>> X30.4 Y90 Z-800 W50 U90

title: Get Position Offset Command
text: Use PositionOffset to query position information related to the working offset. Its meaning and response format depend on the model. Delta X 1 / Delta X 2 / Delta X S PositionOffset >>> X0.5 Y1.2 Z-2.2 Delta X 3 returns the current XYZ position relative to the working origin set by M206 , in mm with two decimal places. At the working origin, the response is: PositionOffset >>> 0.00,0.00,0.00 With no working origin enabled, X3 returns the same coordinates as Position . Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .

title: Get Current Theta Angles
text: For the current angles of the three upper arms, use Angle (angles in deg). Delta X 1 / Delta X 2 / Delta X S Angle >>> X2.46 Y2.46 Z2.46 Delta X 3 returns Theta1,Theta2,Theta3 in degrees, with two decimal places: Angle >>> 2.46,2.46,2.46 Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .

title: Get Current Endstop Sensor States
text: Read the current states of the three home sensors. HTs >>> 111 Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .

title: Get Robot IMEI
text: To find the robot’s unique IMEI, use the IMEI command. Delta X 1 / Delta X 2 / Delta X S IMEI >>> 0004-0000-0000-0012 Delta X 3 includes the IMEI: prefix: IMEI >>> IMEI:0002-0000-0001 Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .

title: Get Robot Information
text: The Infor command provides details like the model, mainboard version, and firmware version. Delta X S example Infor >>> @IMWI Technology >>> Main_board_version: V1.0 >>> Firmware_version: V1.0 >>> Model: DELTA_XS_V4_D800 Delta X 3 example Infor >>> @Delta X Robotics >>> Main_board_version: V1.02 >>> Firmware_version: 1.08 >>> Model: DELTA_X_3 Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .
syntax: Infor >>> @IMWI Technology >>> Main_board_version: V1.0 >>> Firmware_version: V1.0 >>> Model: DELTA_XS_V4_D800

title: Get Robot Active Status
text: To check the robot’s current status, use DeltaState . Delta X 2: Free , Running , Wait , Almostdone , Done . Delta X 3: Free , Running , Wait , Executed , Done , Stop , SendConfirm . DeltaState >>> Free Model: Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 .

title: Set Feedback String
text: You can customize the feedback message after a command execution by setting a feedback string. Delta X S Feedback: done >>> set feedback string to 'done' Delta X 3 uses uppercase FEEDBACK: followed immediately by 1 to 24 printable ASCII characters. Send this while the robot is idle. The setting is saved to EEPROM, and the reply uses the new string: FEEDBACK:done >>> done Model: Delta X 3 , Delta X S . With Delta X 2 model, this command will be FEEDBACK:<custom_string> .
syntax: Feedback: done >>> set feedback string to 'done'

title: Emergency Stop Command
text: Send an emergency signal with Emergency:<state> . States include Reset, Stop, Pause, or Resume. Emergency:<state> Where <state> can be: Reset - reset robot Stop - stop robot Pause - pause robot Resume - resume robot On Delta X 3 and Delta X S V4/V5 , use the exact forms Emergency:Stop , Emergency:Pause , Emergency:Resume , and Emergency:Reset , with no space after the colon. Stop and Pause interrupt the current movement. Resume clears the software stop/pause condition; it does not continue the interrupted path. Check pending commands before resuming, because Stop does not guarantee that the queue is cleared. For the recovery sequence, queue handling, and controller restart steps, see Emergency stop and recovery in Termite . Model: Delta X 2 , Delta X 3 , Delta X S .

title: Get Current Temperature
text: To get the hot end’s current temperature, use the TempState command. Model: Delta X 2 TempState >>> T:27.3 Model: Delta X 1 Temp >>> T:28.2 Model: Delta X 2

title: Set up WIFI connection
text: For models Delta X 1 and Delta X 2 , use the SSID and PSWD commands to connect to Wi-Fi. The robot will return its IP address upon successful connection. Make sure to switch to WiFi mode . SSID:<wifi_name> PSWD:<wifi_password> IP For Eg: SSID:IMWI wifi >>> Ok PSWD:onlyuknow >>> Ok >>> IP:192.168.233.1 If you forgot your IP: IP >>> IP:192.168.233.1 Model: Delta X 1 , Delta X 2 .

title: Assembly Instructions
page: Delta X S V5 — Assembly guide
text: Before mounting the Delta robot, ensure that the frame or surface you are attaching it to is stable and level. Use a measuring tape and a level to verify the frame’s position. Step 1: Mounting the robot onto the frame On the base of the robot body, there are four Ø8 holes used for attaching the Delta robot body to the frame. Please use M8 bolts to tighten and secure the robot. Step 2: Power on and Home the robot Power on the robot Plug in the Robot Power Cable: Connect the power cable from the power supply unit to the robot’s power input port. Ensure a secure connection. Turn on the Power Supply: Switch the power button on the power supply unit. You should see the power LED confirming that power is flowing. Home the robot Connect the Robot with a Computer: using USB-B cable to the USB0 port on the backside of the robot body. Control robot with Delta X Software : Download the software at our download page address Press Connect button and wait for connection. If the connection is successful, try the Home button, the robot will go home and the first move is done. Step 3: Attaching the arms to the robot body Mounting the Upper Arms to the flanges: DO NOT attempt to rotate the flange if the upper arm is not installed. Use 6x M6x16mm bolts to assemble the upper arm onto the flange, ensuring that the marked surfaces align with each other. Install the Lower Arms and the Moving Base : Pull the lower arm out and position it on the outside of the ball end of the upper arm. Repeat this process with the other two arms. Do the same with moving base: Step 4(Optional): Install Axis 4 (5,6) If the robot has axis 4, assemble the universal joint of axis 4 onto the rotating flange underneath the robot body, ensuring a snug fit. Then, tighten the M3 bolt securely first and then fasten the hex socket set screw M3 . And the basic assembly of the robot is now complete.

title: Step 2: Write the Sketch for Arduino
text: The idea is when the button pressed, the Arduino will create a G-code queue and send it via Serial Port to control the robot drawing the spiral. You can visit my Github to DOWNLOAD the project . To calculate the spiral dimensions, you need to consider both the working range of the robot and the specifications of your own system. Please exercise caution when identifying the z_safe value, ensuring that the end effector does not come into contact with any obstacles along its path. Programming First, we create queues to store G-codes. #include <Arduino.h> #include "Vector/Vector.h" String GcodeArray[20]; String InitGcodeArray[20]; Vector<String> InitGcodeQueue; Vector<String> GcodeQueue; Create init G-code queue, this queue code includes initialization commands, homing, setting feedrate and acceleration, and more. void create_init_gcode_queue() { InitGcodeQueue.push_back("G28"); InitGcodeQueue.push_back("M203 S" + String((int)feedrate)); InitGcodeQueue.push_back("M204 A" + String((int)accel)); InitGcodeQueue.push_back("M205 S" + String(begin_vel)); InitGcodeQueue.push_back("M360 E0"); InitGcodeQueue.push_back("G01 X0 Y0 Z" + String(z_safe)); } Calculate and create a spiral queue: void create_gcode_queue(int start_radius, int stop_radius, int step) { GcodeQueue.push_back("M03"); GcodeQueue.push_back("G01 X" + String(start_radius) + " Y0 Z" + String(z_exe)); int current_x = start_radius; int current_i = start_radius; String gc = ""; while (abs(current_x) <= stop_radius - step) { if (current_x > 0) { current_i = -current_x - step / 2; current_x = -current_x - step; } else { current_i = -current_x + step / 2; current_x = -current_x + step; } gc = "G02 X" + String(current_x) + " Y0 I" + String(current_i) + " J0"; GcodeQueue.push_back(gc); } GcodeQueue.push_back("M05"); GcodeQueue.push_back("G01 X0 Y0 Z" + String(z_safe)); } Then check the button pressing event in loop function: void loop() { if (millis() - lastMillis >= 200) { lastMillis = millis(); if (!digitalRead(2)) { if (stt == FREE) { stt = EXECUTING; create_gcode_queue(start_radius, stop_radius, step); send_exe_gcodes(); } } } ... }

title: Connect to the robot for the first time
text: Power on the robot and its controller, then wait for the robot’s Wi-Fi access point (AP) to appear. On your computer or tablet, open the Wi-Fi list and join the robot’s AP. Its name normally follows DeltaXSmart-xxxx . The default password is 12345678 ; use the configured password if it has been changed. Stay connected even if your device reports that this network has no Internet access. Open http://deltax.com in your browser. DeltaXStudio should appear as shown below.

title: Connect the robot to your Wi-Fi
text: Open WiFi at the upper left of DeltaXStudio, then use Scan WiFi to find and select your network. Enter your Wi-Fi password and click Connect . Wait for the connection to succeed. At the top of the window, check that Connected WiFi shows your network name and Local IP shows an IP address. Write down Local IP before switching your computer to another network. In this screenshot, the robot has joined Delta X Lab_5G and its Local IP is 192.168.50.231 . Your network name and IP address will be different. Use Local IP for access through your Wi-Fi; the address under Access belongs to the robot’s AP.

title: Open DeltaXStudio through your Wi-Fi
text: Connect your computer or tablet to the same Wi-Fi network as the robot. In your browser, enter http://<Local IP>:3000 , replacing <Local IP> with the address you wrote down. For the screenshot above, the address is http://192.168.50.231:3000 . Confirm that DeltaXStudio opens. You can now access the robot through your own network. The standard web port is 3000 ; use the port supplied with your installation if it differs. After switching to your Wi-Fi, use the robot’s IP address instead of deltax.com . Once IP access works, you can turn off Enable AP in the WiFi window if you no longer need the robot’s hotspot.

title: Find the main controls
text: Once connected, use the navigation to work through the setup: Area Use Dashboard View the robot, camera, conveyor, and operating status. Settings → System Configure the installed hardware, robot, vision, and startup behavior. Settings → Calibration Run the guided camera and robot calibration. Settings → Parameters Set pick and place positions, motion parameters, and object selections. Vision Capture images for labeling and training in DeltaXHub, or prepare template images for detection. Programs Create, check, save, and run Blockly tasks. Keep Auto Start disabled while setting up the system. After changing settings, click Save and wait for confirmation. When a configuration change requires a restart, stop the running task first, then use Settings → System → System Control → Reset and wait for the interface to reconnect.

title: Check the installed hardware
text: Open Settings → System and review Hardware Settings . Enable the devices actually installed, including the main camera and, for a conveyor setup, the conveyor and encoder. Check the installed camera, encoder, conveyor, and tool outputs. The selected devices and numeric values are examples; use the hardware fitted to your installation. In Robot Settings , check the robot model and its detected address. The robot address identifies the robot controller; it is separate from the Wi-Fi Local IP used to open the web page. Check the end-effector type and output configuration for your vacuum tool or gripper. Verify the model and controller address for each robot. This address is separate from the web interface IP. Save the settings and return to Dashboard . Confirm that the intended robot is connected and that the camera produces a current image. For a conveyor system, confirm that encoder readings respond to conveyor movement before starting calibration. A working web page confirms access to DeltaXStudio; check the device status separately before sending robot commands. If an advanced setting is hidden, switch the settings view from Basic to Advanced .

title: Ready for calibration
text: Continue when the intended robot and camera respond correctly, and the encoder responds to conveyor movement if your setup uses tracking. Then calibrate the camera and robot coordinates .

title: If you cannot connect
text: Problem What to check The robot AP is missing Check power and wait for the controller to start, then refresh your device’s Wi-Fi list. deltax.com does not open Make sure you are connected to the robot’s AP and enter http://deltax.com explicitly. Stay on the AP if your device warns about no Internet access. The robot cannot join your Wi-Fi Check the selected network and password, move within signal range, and scan again. The AP disconnects during setup Join your own Wi-Fi and find the robot controller’s IP in the router’s connected-device list. The IP address does not open Confirm that your computer and robot are on the same network. Check the current Local IP and include the web port, normally 3000 . A previously working bookmark stops opening Your router may have assigned a new IP address. Check the controller’s current address in the router, or through the robot AP if it is available.

title: Before you start
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Prepare an assembled, securely mounted robot, its power supply, a USB data cable, and a Windows computer. Clear the robot’s working area before homing or moving it, and keep its physical emergency-stop control accessible. Choose the command reference that matches your robot: Robot G-code reference Delta X 3, firmware < 2.0.0 X3 G-code Delta X 3, firmware > 2.0.0 New firmware reference — being prepared Delta X S V4 XS V4 G-code Delta X S V5 XS V5 G-code The command examples below follow the existing X3 reference and the XS V4/V5 references. For the new X3 firmware, use the commands provided with that firmware until its reference is available.

title: 1. Open Termite
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Download Termite from the official CompuPhase download page , install or extract it, and open the application. The large area displays communication with the robot. Type commands in the narrow entry field at the bottom and press Enter to send them.

title: 2. Connect the robot and find its COM port
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Connect the robot’s USB control port to the computer with the USB data cable. Robot USB port Computer USB port Turn on the robot’s power supply. USB communication alone does not supply power for robot movement. Close other applications using the robot’s serial port, such as another terminal or control application. Open Windows Device Manager , then expand Ports (COM & LPT) . Note the robot’s COM number. You can unplug and reconnect the USB cable to identify the entry that disappears and returns. This screenshot shows USB-SERIAL CH340 (COM5) . The device name and COM number may differ on your computer; use the port identified for your robot.

title: 3. Configure the serial connection
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Click Settings and use these values: Setting Value Port The robot’s COM port from Device Manager Baud rate 115200 Data bits 8 Stop bits 1 Parity none Flow control none Forward none Transmitted text Append CR-LF Local echo Checked, to display the commands you send COM5 is the example port shown in these screenshots. Select the port assigned to your robot in Device Manager. Click OK . If the status still reads Disconnected - click to connect , click that status field to open the port.

title: 4. Check communication
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Enter the following command in the bottom field and press Enter : IsDelta The robot should reply with YesDelta . With local echo enabled, your typed command also appears in the receive area; that echoed line alone does not confirm a connection. Then send: Infor Check the returned robot model and firmware version against the reference selected above.

title: 5. Home the robot
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Make sure the robot can complete its homing movement, then send: G28 Wait for homing to finish and for the completion reply, normally Ok , before sending a movement command. If the robot reports an error, resolve it before continuing. Read the current position with: Position The response format depends on the robot. X3 returns comma-separated XYZ coordinates; see Useful Commands for the model-specific formats.

title: 6. Try a small movement
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Use absolute positioning to move the tool to specific coordinates. In this mode, X , Y , and Z are target positions in the robot’s current coordinate system, measured in millimeters. Send one line at a time and wait for Ok before the next line. Do not paste the entire sequence into the command field at once. After completing homing in step 5, select absolute positioning: G90 G90 selects the coordinate mode; it does not move the robot. Move to a starting position Choose one starting command for your robot. The examples use Z-360 for X3 and Z-750 from the XS G-code reference. For XS, check the workspace of your specific size and adjust Z before sending the command; Z-750 is not a common working height for every XS model. Confirm that the path to the starting position and the following 10 mm X movement are clear. If you have configured coordinate offsets, account for them when choosing the target. Delta X 3: move to the absolute position (0, 0, -360) : G01 X0 Y0 Z-360 F100 A1000 J10000 S0 E0 Delta X S: move to the absolute position (0, 0, -750) , using a Z value appropriate to your model: G01 X0 Y0 Z-750 F100 A1000 J10000 S0 E0 The starting command sets the feed rate to 100 mm/s, acceleration to 1000 mm/s², jerk to 10000 mm/s³, and start/end velocities to zero. These motion settings remain in effect for subsequent moves until changed; you only need to enter them once. Move along X and return For either robot, send: G01 X10 This moves to the absolute coordinate X = 10 mm , keeping Y and Z at the starting values. Sending G01 X10 again keeps the same target; it does not add another 10 mm. Return to X = 0 mm : G01 X0 The tool is now back at the starting position you selected above, with the same Y and Z. Absolute positioning remains active for the next movement commands. The screenshot shows a test using Z-650 for that setup, followed by G1 X10 and G1 X0 . Choose Z for your own robot as described above. G90 is not shown in the screenshot; send it before the movement commands to select absolute positioning.

title: 7. Emergency stop and recovery
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Use Emergency:Stop when you need to interrupt robot movement because of an emergency. Enter the command in Termite and press Enter immediately; do not wait for the current movement’s Ok reply. Emergency:Stop The firmware replies Delta:Stop . Check that the robot has stopped, and stop sending movement commands. A serial emergency stop depends on the USB connection and firmware; use the physical emergency stop when immediate intervention is needed. Write these commands exactly as shown, with no space after the colon. Command Purpose Emergency:Stop Request an emergency stop and interrupt movement. Emergency:Resume Clear the software stop/pause condition so commands can run again. It does not restart the interrupted path from the stopping point. Emergency:Pause Request a pause. On the X3 and XS firmware covered by this guide, this also interrupts the active path; it is not a pause-and-continue function for that path. Emergency:Reset Restart the robot controller. Use it when a controller restart is required, then reconnect and home again. Recover after an emergency stop Identify and resolve the cause of the stop. Check the tool, workpiece, and robot’s position, then clear the working area. If the physical emergency-stop button was pressed, release it only after the cause has been resolved. A serial Resume command does not release the physical button. Confirm that no unwanted commands are waiting to run. The examples in this guide send one movement at a time. If you previously sent several movements ahead, follow Clear pending commands before resuming. Send: Emergency:Resume XS replies Delta:Resume ; X3 uses its configured completion reply, normally Ok . Resume allows commands to run again; it does not confirm the robot’s position or home it. Check that the homing path is clear, then send: G28 Wait for homing to finish before sending the next command. Re-homing is especially necessary if the stop interrupted homing, the motors were disabled, or the mechanism was moved. Restore absolute positioning and check the position, sending each line separately: G90 Position Review the next target and motion settings, then send a new movement command when ready. Do not assume the interrupted move reached its original target. Clear pending commands Emergency:Stop does not guarantee that queued commands have been cleared. Resume may allow pending commands to execute. On XS V5 , after the robot has stopped and before Resume, you can discard pending G-code commands with: Robot:QueueClear This clears waiting commands; it does not stop an active movement. It is not available in the X3 or XS V4 firmware covered here. For X3 or XS V4 , if you are unsure which commands remain queued, use the controller restart procedure below instead of resuming that queue. Pause and resume To request a pause, send: Emergency:Pause The firmware replies Delta:Pause . Before sending Emergency:Resume , review the robot state and any pending commands as described above. Send a new target for the next movement; Resume does not complete the interrupted path automatically. Restart the controller When a controller restart is required, first stop movement and stop sending commands, then send: Emergency:Reset The firmware replies Delta:Reset and restarts. The USB connection may disconnect; wait for the controller to restart, then reconnect Termite if needed. Send IsDelta to check communication, run G28 after checking the homing path, and select G90 before using the absolute movement examples again. Re-enter any settings that were not saved before the restart.

title: 8. Disconnect normally
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Let the current movement finish, then click Termite’s connection status field to close the COM port, or close Termite. You do not need Emergency:Stop just to disconnect after normal operation. Closing the terminal does not stop a movement already executing.

title: Troubleshooting
page: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite
text: Symptom What to check The robot does not appear in Device Manager Check power, the USB data cable, and the USB port. If Windows reports a driver issue, install the driver appropriate to the robot’s USB interface. Termite cannot open the COM port Select the correct port and close any other application using it. The sent command appears, but there is no robot reply Check that the port is connected, the baud rate is 115200 , and Append CR-LF is selected. Local echo is not a reply from the robot. The received text is unreadable Check the baud rate, data bits, parity, and stop bits against the settings above. IsDelta works but the robot will not move Check motor power and the stop state. If stopped, follow Emergency stop and recovery , then home with G28 and read any returned error. A movement command is rejected Check the command reference for the installed firmware, the current G90/G91 mode, and the robot’s workspace. For further commands, use the matching X3 reference , XS V4 reference , or XS V5 reference .

text: Control Delta X 3 and Delta X S with Termite Use Termite on Windows to send text commands to your robot through its USB serial connection. This guide takes you from selecting the COM port to homing and a short movement test. Before you start Prepare an assembled, securely mounted robot, its power supply, a USB data cable, and a Windows computer. Clear the robot’s working area before homing or moving it, and keep its physical emergency-stop contro

title: Start a program
text: Open Programs and select the Blockly view. Click New for an empty workspace, or open Templates and choose a starting program. Save any changes you want to keep before replacing the current workspace. Template Starting point What to configure Stationary pick & place One pick followed by one place. Pick and place poses, working heights, and end effector. Conveyor pick & place A detection loop with an empty-result check and tracking configuration. Encoder direction, tracker selection, tooling, and pick/place inputs. Sort two object types Separate branches for class indices 0 and 1 . Class mapping, destinations, tooling, and tracking when objects move. Template vision frame A per-frame vision workspace. Image processing, the actual template folder, and detection settings. Templates are editable drafts. Loading one does not start the robot, and required inputs may be intentionally empty. Fill them for your installation before running. Click Use template beside the example you want. Save the completed program under your own task name.

title: Build with blocks
text: Drag a block from the toolbox into the workspace. Connect action blocks in the order they should execute, and fit value blocks into inputs such as positions, numbers, or conditions. Use loops for repeated work and conditions to decide whether an action should run. Toolbox group Use it for Robot Control → Movement Robot movement and pick/place actions. Robot Control → IO & Settings End-effector setup, I/O, and robot settings. Vision → Objects Retrieve detected objects and read their properties. Vision → Image Proc / Detection / Drawing Process camera images, detect objects, and draw the preview. Conveyor Control Conveyor operation and tracking setup. Loops / Logic Repetition, conditions, and comparisons. Math / Variables Calculations and values reused by later blocks. Connect the blocks that belong to the same sequence and fill their required inputs. Check the units shown on each block. End-effector delays in blocks use milliseconds, while the parameter panels use Dwell in seconds: 100 ms equals 0.1 s . An end effector, shown as EE , grips and releases the object. A Tracker follows a moving object using the configured conveyor/encoder. Fill an empty input To fill a height or another numeric input, open Math , drag the number block into its white socket until it snaps in, then click its number to enter a value. Click a dropdown to choose an existing end effector, tracker, or object type. Open Math and drag the number block marked 0 into the required numeric socket. For a fixed Obj Pos , open Vision → Objects and drag Object Pos from into the input. Fit number blocks into its X, Y, and Angle inputs. This block only groups three entered values; it does not require Vision AI. For a detected object, use Get Object Pos from the object variable instead. Z Move and Z Pick/Z Place remain separate height inputs. Movement X, Y, and Z values use millimetres in robot coordinates; Angle uses degrees. Measure these for the installed tool. Values in the screenshots illustrate one installation. To reuse a value, open Variables → Create variable and enter its name. The set … to block stores a value; the small variable block reads it later. For motion settings, set F, A, J, S, and E once before the repeated picking sequence; they continue to apply until changed. Input How to choose it EE Select the tool ID defined by Configure End Effectors, such as 0 , on both pick and place. Tracker Select the configured tracker for a moving pickup; use None for a fixed position. Obj Pos Fixed [X, Y, Angle] values, or Get Object Pos from a detected object. Z Move A measured transfer height that clears the carried object and fixtures. Z Pick / Z Place The measured tool height for gripping/releasing the object.

title: Check and save
text: Click Check program to check the draft before saving. Read the reported issues and use Locate block , when available, to find the block that needs attention. A passed check does not verify physical clearance or values calculated while the task runs. A passed static check verifies the program structure. Check motion values and physical clearance separately. Enter a task name and click Save . When editing a saved task, use Update . Wait for the saved confirmation and check that no unsaved changes remain. Selecting a task in Saved Tasks loads it for editing. An existing task shows Editing and Update. A new task uses the name field and Save.

title: Run and stop a task
text: Before the first run, check the target robot, tool operation, coordinates, and clearance. Keep Auto Start disabled while developing the program. For picking, begin with one object and conservative motion settings. Open Programs and find your saved task in Saved Tasks . Clicking its name opens the blocks for editing. Click its green triangular play button to prepare a run. In Select Target Robots , select the intended robot. For the first test, use one robot whose setup you have checked. Click Run Task and observe the result. While the task runs, its play button changes to a square Stop task button. Use that button to end the test before making changes. The trash button deletes the saved program. Use the green triangle beside your task name to open robot selection. Select the robot that should execute your program, then click Run Task when ready for the test. The robot name shown is an example. A robot already running another task is shown as busy. Do not start Main Task alongside a custom movement task for the same robot. The header Run button starts the task selected in Run Button Task ; it does not simply run whichever program is open in the editor. Use the physical emergency stop when immediate intervention is needed. After a normal test, stop the task, edit the blocks, check the program, and update the saved task before running again.

title: Program examples
text: Choose an example after learning the editor controls above. Start with Stationary pick & place for your first movement program. Continue with a camera-based example once the robot, tool, and fixed-position cycle work. Movement examples These programs move the robot. Set the poses, heights, and tool for your installation before running. Example Vision AI Position source and next skill Stationary pick & place Not required Enter fixed pick and place positions; test one cycle. Conveyor pick & place (AI) Enabled Retrieve AI detections and track pickup with the encoder. Color filtering + pick & place Disabled Detect objects by HSV and pick them in one combined task. Test the vision-only color example first. Sort two object types (AI) Enabled Branch on two trained AI classes and place them at separate destinations. Camera-based picking requires completed Calibration and a working Vision method. Conveyor pickup also requires encoder feedback. Vision-only examples These tasks process camera images and send detections to tracking. Keep movement tasks stopped while testing their previews. Example Vision AI What to test Color filtering Disabled HSV mask, object outlines, and tracking output. Color + Template Matching Disabled Color candidates refined against reference images. The Vision setup guides explain how to prepare and tune each method. These examples show the actual blocks and their connections. After detection works, choose the picking task for your application.

title: Enable Vision AI for movement examples
text: Use AI for the Conveyor and Sort examples. Their guides include the model selection, main enable switch, Save System step, and detection check: Set up Conveyor pick & place with AI . Set up AI for sorting two object types . Keep Vision AI disabled for the color pipelines. Fixed-position Stationary pick & place does not require AI. Find the Vision AI and Template Matching switches Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . The switch beside the heading enables AI; the separate Filter switch controls object-size filtering. Click Save System after changing the configuration. This screenshot shows AI Disabled. Enable it for AI movement examples; keep it Disabled for the color pipelines.

title: Create a picking loop
text: Configure the end effector before the loop. For moving objects, also configure tracking and verify the encoder direction and selected tracker. Set the pick, place, and transfer heights for the installed tool and object; see Pick & Place parameters . Inside the loop, use Get Object in Robot Area and store the result in a variable. Check that the result is not None before reading its properties. In that branch, use Get Object Pos to supply the detected pose to Move Pick , then use Move Place with the configured destination, end effector, and tracker. When no object is available, skip the movement branch. Include a short wait in the loop before requesting the next object. The conveyor template provides this structure so you can adapt the inputs rather than assemble it from scratch. For sorting, branch on the detected object type and provide a destination for each class to be handled. Verify the class indices against the final Vision output, particularly when Template Matching supplies the object type. Keep movement inside the object-found condition so an empty lookup skips the pick.

title: Combine Vision and movement
text: With Vision AI enabled and verified , a movement task retrieves the tracked objects directly. The conveyor and AI sorting examples use this arrangement. For color filtering, disable Vision AI and the System Template Matching switch, click Save System, and build the image-processing pipeline in Blockly using the matching guide: Color filtering Color + Template Matching Put the image pipeline inside Vision in main flow and keep the movement loop outside it. The final detections must reach Convert To Tracking Object and Push To Tracking Manager so that the movement loop can retrieve them. Test the vision-only task and inspect its preview before adding robot movement. Drawing boxes on an image alone does not make the objects available for picking.
