The parameter and destination sections below describe the built-in Main Task.

title: Configure the pick and place parameters
text: For built-in Main Task , open Settings → Parameters . If there are multiple robots, select the robot whose parameters you want to edit. Setting What to enter Pick Parameters → Pick Z (mm) The tool height at which the object is picked, in robot coordinates. Pick Parameters → Dwell (s) The time allowed for the end effector to grip the object before lifting. Place Parameters → Place Z (mm) The tool height at which the object is released. Place Parameters → Dwell (s) The time allowed for release before moving away. Other Parameters → Travel Z (mm) The transfer height between pick and place, with clearance for the object, fixtures, and destination. Motion parameters Feedrate F in mm/s, acceleration A in mm/s², jerk J in mm/s³, and start/end speeds S/E in mm/s. Keep start/end speeds within the selected feedrate. Robot Pick Area The part of the tracked working area assigned to this robot. Pick Z, Place Z, and Travel Z are absolute robot-coordinate heights. Determine them for the installed tool and object; values from another robot or a sample program may not fit your machine. Check the end-effector type and output configuration in Settings → System . Save the parameter changes and wait for the saved confirmation before running. Set pickup height, grip dwell, and motion for the installed robot and tool. Use measured values rather than copying the screenshot. Travel Z is an absolute transfer height in robot coordinates. Conveyor Z records the measured belt surface. Configure the tracked picking region assigned to this robot and check it against the calibrated workspace.

title: Assign object types to place destinations
text: For built-in Main Task, start with the point-based place mode and configure Place candidates under Place Parameters. Match each Object index to the class order in Vision AI Objects: index 0 is the first class, index 1 the second. Enter the destination X , Y , and Angle for each class you want to place. Use + Object type to add another class. The plus button on a row adds another candidate destination for that same class. Each Object index has its own destination candidates. Add only indices used by your model and enter reachable positions for your installation. Under Pick Objects Index → Config , select the classes this robot should pick. Save and verify the class-to-destination mapping using one object from each selected class. Choose which trained classes may be picked. All objects includes every class; the names shown are examples. To skip a class, exclude it from the pick selection. In point-based placement, an object without a valid place candidate is also skipped. Preserve the other class indices when removing candidates; do not remove a class name from the Vision AI Objects list to skip it. An empty Pick Objects Index setting means all classes. Do not use an empty setting as a way to disable picking.

title: Make the first pick
text: Use this procedure for built-in Main Task . For a Blockly task, follow the run procedure in its selected example. Confirm that calibration is complete, the intended model or vision program is active, and the camera recognizes a test object correctly. Check the pick height, transfer clearance, destination, and end-effector operation. Open Settings → System → System Control . Set Run Button Task to Main Task and save. Return to Dashboard and click Run to start the built-in pick-and-place task. For a conveyor setup, start the conveyor at a low test speed and introduce one object. Observe the pick, transfer, and release. Stop the task before adjusting parameters. Repeat with each object class and several positions before increasing throughput. Use the normal task Stop control to end a test. If immediate intervention is required, use the physical emergency stop. Select Main Task for Run Button Task during the built-in picking test. Keep Auto Start Disabled while commissioning.

title: Correct picking and release errors
text: The tool consistently misses by the same amount Open Settings → Parameters → Pick Parameters → Robot Center Offset . Apply the correction in robot X/Y coordinates. For example, if the tool is consistently 5 mm too far in negative X and 3 mm too far in positive Y, the required correction is +5 mm in X and −3 mm in Y. Add this correction to the current offset, save, and test again. Use Object Center Offset when the desired grip point is displaced from the detected object center and that displacement should follow the object’s rotation. Leave it at zero when picking at the detected center. If the error changes with conveyor speed, object position, or rotation, check tracking, calibration, and orientation first. A fixed Robot Center Offset cannot correct all of those errors. The tool reaches the object but does not hold it Check Pick Z, tool contact, vacuum or gripper operation, and the configured output. If the tool needs more time to grip, increase Pick Parameters → Dwell (s) gradually. Keep the delay only as long as needed for reliable pickup. The object is still attached when the robot leaves Check the release output and tool operation. Increase Place Parameters → Dwell (s) if the object needs more time to release before the robot moves away. A detected object is not picked Check that its class is included in Pick Objects Index, it has a valid destination, it enters Robot Pick Area, and the selected task is running on the intended robot. For vision blocks, also check that detections reach Push To Tracking Manager .

title: Enable automatic startup
text: Enable automatic startup only after the selected task has passed manual tests with the installed hardware and workspace clear. Open Settings → System → System Control . Set Auto Run Task to Main Task or the saved program that should start after power-up. Enable Auto Start , then save and wait for confirmation. Enable Auto Start only after manual tests pass. Auto Run Task selects the startup program; Run Button Task controls the header button. Test a controlled restart with the work area clear. The controller attempts automatic startup approximately 15 seconds after its application starts, subject to its connection and run-state checks. Auto Run Task is separate from Run Button Task. Check both selections. A custom automatic-start task is dispatched to the configured robots, so verify the program is suitable for every target in a multi-robot installation. Turn Auto Start off and save before returning to setup or changing the application.

title: Setup complete
text: The setup is ready for routine operation when low-speed tests reliably pick, transfer, and release each selected object class at several positions. For conveyor applications, verify tracking as well. Continue with Daily Operation for normal startup, checks, and stopping. To customize the application, use Blockly Programming . This is optional when the built-in task meets your needs.

title: Prepare the vision task
text: Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Set the main Vision AI switch to Disabled and also disable the System Template Matching switch. Click Save System and wait for confirmation. To locate the switches, open Find the Vision AI and Template Matching switches and expand the screenshot. Open Programs. Load Docs_ColorFiltering_Draft if it is already in Saved Tasks, or click New and build the sequence shown below. Add Vision → Image Proc → Vision in main flow and connect the image-processing blocks inside it. Use Variables → Create variable to add the names listed in the table below. Use a set block to store each result and the corresponding small variable block as the input to the following step. Keep the robot movement program stopped until you have tested this vision-only task and its preview.

title: Block program
text: Docs_ColorFiltering_Draft: color filtering inside Vision in main flow. Click the image to inspect the blocks. Place the image-processing sequence inside Vision in main flow . Use variables to pass each result to the next block: Variable in the image What it contains Used by _croppe_image The calibrated detection image, later replaced by the annotated preview. Filter HSV, Draw Rotated Objects To Image, Set Preview Image. hsv_image The binary mask produced by Filter HSV and updated by the two Denoise Image blocks. Find Contours. new_contours Contours that pass the size limits. Find Rotation Objects From Contours. new_objs Candidate objects with centers, sizes, and angles. Drawing and Convert To Tracking Object. tracking_objs Objects converted for the tracking manager. Push To Tracking Manager. The drawing block uses the original detection image and new_objs . Send tracking_objs to tracking, then use the annotated _croppe_image as the preview. Variable names can differ, but the connections must preserve this flow.

title: Values shown in the image
text: Block setting Screenshot value How to use it Lower HSV / upper HSV [0,0,26] / [179,255,255] Accepts the full hue and saturation ranges while rejecting very dark pixels. Narrow the bounds for the actual object color and background. Morphology Close / Open Kernel size 1 for both A 1 × 1 kernel does not meaningfully clean the mask. Increase only as needed while inspecting the mask; excessive filtering can merge or distort objects. Find Contours Min area 20 , max area 200 Despite the field names, the current implementation checks both dimensions of each contour’s rotated bounding rectangle, in pixels. Both dimensions must be between 20 and 200 for this example. Convert To Tracking Object Object Type 0 All accepted objects from this pipeline use type 0. Use this same index in pick selection and placement logic. Push To Tracking Manager Filter unchecked The supplied example leaves this option off. These are the values in this screenshot, not universal detection settings. The white-object HSV example in the Vision guide uses different bounds for a different detection target.

title: Check the result
text: Click Check program and correct any missing connections. Enter your own task name, such as My_ColorFiltering , click Save, and wait for confirmation. In Saved Tasks, click the green triangular play button beside your saved task, select the intended robot, and click Run Task. The run controls show these buttons. This task processes images and contains no movement actions. Open the camera preview on Dashboard by clicking the camera in the scene. Temporarily connect hsv_image to Set Preview Image so you can see which pixels pass the filter. Stop the task before editing; Check program, Update, and restart it after changing the preview connection. Objects should form separate filled regions against the background. Restore _croppe_image as the preview after tuning. Check for one stable outline per object and no false objects on an empty background. If an object disappears, inspect the mask and size limits; if one object becomes several, inspect gaps and noise in the mask. Once detection works, follow Color filtering + pick & place to combine this pipeline and a picking loop in one task. Keep Vision AI disabled. If you prefer built-in picking, use the vision-only task with Main Task instead. Choose the robot for this saved task before clicking Run Task. The robot name shown is an example.

title: Image processing
page: Blockly example — Color filtering + pick & place
text: The vision section detects objects and supplies them to tracking. The camera pipeline reads Get Detecting Image, applies Filter HSV and the two Denoise Image blocks, finds contours, and converts them to rotated objects. Use Draw Rotated Objects To Image and Set Preview Image to display the result. The color-filtering example explains each variable and connection. Pass new_objs through Convert To Tracking Object with Object Type 0 . Store the result in tracking_objs and connect that variable to Push To Tracking Manager . These two blocks make detections available to the picking loop; drawing outlines alone does not supply objects for pickup. The captured draft uses lower HSV [0,0,154] and upper HSV [179,124,255] , selecting bright pixels with low saturation. Its contour size limits are 20 – 200 pixels on both rotated bounding-box dimensions, and both morphology kernels are 1 . Use your tested settings rather than copying these values for a different object or background. See Verify color detection for detection adjustments.

title: Tool, tracking, and initialization
page: Blockly example — Color filtering + pick & place
text: The movement setup follows the vision wrapper, outside its image-processing body. Configure End Effectors defines tool 0 : a vacuum tool on pin 0 , with 100 ms grip/release delays and zero X/Y offsets in the screenshot. Set the pin, delays, and offsets for your installed tool. Select that tool ID as EE on both Move Pick and Move Place. Configure Tracking Parameters defines tracker 0 with Use Main Encoder selected and direction angle 0° . Match the direction to your calibrated conveyor. With Use Main Encoder selected, the encoder supplies the conveyor movement; the displayed Speed value is not a command to run the conveyor. The next block assigns PlacePosition = [100, 100, 0] using Object Pos from. This defines the fixed placement X, Y, and Angle. Home the robot and set motion parameters before the first test. To include this preparation in the program, add Go Home and Set Motion Params from Robot Control → Movement before the repeat loop. Enter F, A, J, S, and E once; they continue to apply to later movements until changed.

title: Picking loop
page: Blockly example — Color filtering + pick & place
text: Read objects supplied by the color pipeline, then pick and place when one is available. Inside repeat while true, set detected_object to Get Object in Robot Area . Select Object Type 0 to retrieve the objects produced by this pipeline. The screenshot shows None , which accepts any available type. The condition if detected_object means “an object was found.” Keep the pick and place actions inside this condition so an empty lookup skips movement. Input Value shown Move Pick → Obj Pos Get Object Pos from detected_object , as shown. Move Pick → EE / Tracker EE 0 , Tracker 0 for encoder-tracked pickup. Move Pick → Z Move / Z Pick -650 / -700 : transfer and pickup heights. Move Place → Obj Pos PlacePosition, assigned [100, 100, 0] before the loop. Move Place → EE / Tracker EE 0 to release the same tool; Tracker None for the fixed destination. Move Place → Z Move / Z Place -650 / -690 : transfer and release heights. Measure the heights and destination for your installation before replacing these values. Use number blocks from Math for height inputs. To define PlacePosition, create the variable under Variables, connect Vision → Objects → Object Pos from to its set block, and fill X, Y, and Angle. Connect a PlacePosition variable block to Move Place → Obj Pos. This position block does not enable or require AI. See Fill an empty input and Pick & Place parameters for the inputs and height meanings. After placement, the loop requests another object. If no object is available, it skips the movement branch and tries again.

text: Complete and test the color-filtering program first so you can see the candidate objects before adding matching. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Set the main Vision AI switch and the separate Template Matching switch to Disabled , then click Save System . To locate the switches, open Find the Vision AI and Template Matching switches and expand the screenshot. Prepare a template folder containing cropped reference images for your objects. The screenshot selects default ; choose a folder containing the reference images prepared for your objects.

title: Block program
text: Docs_ColorTemplateMatching_Draft captured in DeltaXStudio. Select your prepared template folder and tune the filter values for your objects. Keep the image read, HSV filter, denoising, contour extraction, and Find Rotation Objects From Contours blocks from the color example. Insert Match With Template after candidate-object extraction. In this program, its output is assigned back to new_objs , replacing the candidate list with the matched list. Connection Value to use Match With Template objects input new_objs , the candidate objects from contours. Draw Rotated Objects To Image objects input new_objs , after the matching assignment. title: Configure the match
text: Select the actual template folder in Match With Template, then set its threshold and scale. A higher threshold is stricter and may reject valid objects as well as unwanted ones. The block’s scale is a percentage: 25% corresponds to 0.25 in System settings. The screenshot selects folder default , threshold 0.65 , and scale 25% . Choose your own prepared template folder and tune these values against representative images. The HSV, contour, and denoising settings are inherited from the color-filtering example . text: Stop running tasks and keep Auto Start disabled. Check the robot and main camera connections. Confirm the encoder counts increase with forward conveyor travel. title: Check the working height
text: Open Settings → Parameters and select the intended robot if more than one is configured. With the conveyor stopped, use the Dashboard robot controls to approach the belt surface with the installed tool. Reduce the jog increment near the surface and avoid pressing the tool into the belt. text: Stop running tasks and keep Auto Start disabled. Check the robot and main camera connections. Confirm the encoder counts increase with forward conveyor travel. Disable Calibration Camera in Hardware Settings. Select Camera Fov outside robot area and disable Use Conveyor in Calibration Settings. Keep the encoder connected. Check the working heights, save, reset, and wait for reconnection. Use Conveyor is disabled; also disable Calibration Camera for this setup. Keep Calibration Camera disabled when capturing robot points manually. The encoder is still required for this conveyor method.

title: Check the working height
text: Open Settings → Parameters and select the intended robot if more than one is configured. With the conveyor stopped, use the Dashboard robot controls to approach the belt surface with the installed tool. Reduce the jog increment near the surface and avoid pressing the tool into the belt. Read the robot’s Z coordinate at the belt surface and enter it in Other Parameters → Conveyor Z (mm) . This is the field called Z Conveyor in the reference manual. Set Travel Z (mm) , called Z Move in the manual, to a height that clears the carried object, belt, fixtures, and destination throughout the transfer. Save the settings before calibration. Automatic calibration uses Conveyor Z to calculate approach positions, so check this value for each configured robot. Enter the measured conveyor-surface Z and a transfer Z with adequate clearance. The pictured values illustrate one installation. Read the current Z coordinate while positioning the installed tool. Three object heights above the belt can be used as an initial estimate for Travel Z. For example, a belt at Z = -740 mm and a 20 mm object gives -740 + 3 x 20 = -680 mm . Verify the actual clearance and robot reach; this estimate does not account for every tool or fixture. If a jog command is rejected, check the displayed status, homing state, and configured travel limits before continuing.

title: Place the board and select the crop
text: Stop the conveyor and place the supplied board flat under the main camera. Align it with the belt and leave enough travel for the capture sequence. Check that the whole board is visible, sharp, and well lit. Open Settings → Calibration and click Start . Follow any board-orientation guidance. Select two opposite corners of the detection area in the corrected image. Cover the useful conveyor area. Exclude blank image padding. Click Apply . The system is now ready to capture the reference points. Keep the board aligned with the belt. X Offset describes the conveyor centerline relative to the robot. Select the useful detection area, then click Apply. Let the conveyor carry the board between points. Do not lift, slide, or rotate it relative to the belt.

title: Capture the reference points
text: Start and stop the belt using its own controls whenever the screen requests it. Use a low speed, approximately 20-30 mm/s , for these positioning steps. At Find Robot Point 1 , follow the prompt to bring the board into reach, then stop the conveyor. Use the Dashboard robot controls to align the tool center directly above the board center without touching it. Wait for motion to finish and click Get Point . Move the conveyor again only when prompted. At Find Robot Point 2 , stop the belt and align the robot with the board center at its new position. Capture the second point, repeat for any remaining robots, and wait for successful completion before clicking Done . Both belt positioning and robot-point alignment are manual in this method. Keep the board fixed relative to the belt and capture each point only after the encoder readings are stable. Align the tool center with the board center. Keep the tool clear of the board while aligning.

title: Confirm calibration
text: Wait for successful completion; the system validates and saves the reference points. Click Done , then check the corrected image and crop. Wait for successful completion before clicking Done. Continue to Vision to verify detection before the first pick. During the first low-speed picking test, check several object positions and conveyor tracking. Repeat calibration after moving the camera, robot, or conveyor relative to one another.

title: If this calibration cannot finish
text: Symptom What to check Board not detected Focus, lighting, board orientation, and complete board visibility. Crop rejected Select a non-empty area inside the valid corrected image. Missing or reversed encoder feedback Check the connection and counting direction. Encoder feedback is required for this method. Board passes the capture area Check available travel and camera-to-robot spacing. Reduce belt positioning speed and stop when prompted. Get Point unavailable or rejected Confirm a manual-point step is active, the robot is connected, and motion has finished with a stationary belt. Browser reconnects Wait for the current session state to reload before continuing. Use Stop or Cancel to end the workflow and wait for stopping to finish. Stop an external conveyor using its own controls. Calibration Stop waits for robot motion already in progress; use the physical emergency stop if immediate intervention is needed.

title: Configure this setup
text: Stop running tasks and keep Auto Start disabled. Check the robot and main camera connections. Select Camera Fov in robot area in Calibration Settings. Disable Use Conveyor and Calibration Camera . Save, reset the system, and wait for the main camera and robot to reconnect. Static calibration: also disable Calibration Camera. Use the main camera and keep Calibration Camera disabled for the stationary-board workflow.

title: Check the working height
text: Fit the intended tool and confirm both reference points are within robot reach. Use small jog increments near the working surface. Keep the tool above the board during point alignment; it does not need to touch it. Use the coordinate readout while aligning the tool. Keep the board stationary and the tool clear of its surface. The board must stay fixed throughout both point captures. Establish the later Pick Z and Place Z separately when setting up Pick & Place.

title: Place the board and select the crop
text: Place the board flat in the common camera and robot working area. Both reference points must be reachable. Check that the whole board is visible, sharp, and well lit. Open Settings → Calibration and click Start . Follow any board-orientation guidance. Select two opposite corners of the detection area in the corrected image. Keep this area within robot reach. Exclude blank image padding. Click Apply . The system is now ready to capture the reference points. Place the board within camera view and robot reach. Capture the P1 and P2 markers selected in the current interface. Select the useful detection area, then click Apply. Keep the board completely stationary.

title: Capture the reference points
text: When marker selection appears, select P1 using the displayed board image. The interface calculates the paired P2 . Check the two marker locations and click Submit . At Find Robot Point 1 , jog the tool center above the highlighted P1 marker. Use small increments for final alignment and keep the tool clear of the board. Wait for robot motion to finish, then click Get Point . At Find Robot Point 2 , move the tool to the highlighted P2 marker on the same stationary board and capture the second point. Repeat for additional robots if prompted. Wait for completion and click Done . P1 and P2 are two different markers on a stationary board. Do not move the board or conveyor between captures. If P2 is rejected, check that the tool is aligned with the selected marker and retry. Restart calibration if the board moved or P1 was captured incorrectly.

title: Confirm calibration

Repeat calibration after moving the camera, robot, or conveyor relative to one another.

title: Calibration — Stationary objects
text: Calibration — Stationary objects Calibration · Stationary objects Change method Use this method for stationary objects within both the main camera view and the robot workspace . The belt, if present, remains stopped. Required: robot + main camera . Keep the object and working surface stationary. Screenshots may show an earlier interface; use the field names in the instructions. Configure this setup Stop running tasks and keep Auto Start disabled.

title: Prepare the reference templates
text: Capture templates with the same camera, detection crop, lighting, and object height used during operation. In DeltaXStudio, open Vision and select Template Matching mode. Create or select a template folder. In Images , select Cropped , open the live camera, place a representative object, and click Save Current Image . Choose or create a reference-image folder in Template Matching mode. The pictured folder name is an example. Open Crop and select the saved image. Draw a tight rectangle containing the complete object, with minimal surrounding background. Click Crop & Save . This replaces that saved image with the cropped template; keep training images in their separate AI project. Repeat for the required reference objects. Inspect the folder contents and remove unsuitable captures before using it. Save/apply the configuration and restart the relevant vision task after changing templates. Reset the system if it is still using a previously loaded template set. Check the resulting object index whenever templates supply the type. Template indices follow the loaded filename order, starting at 0 ; they are not automatically matched to AI class names. Keep a clear mapping from each index to its pick filter and place destination, and recheck it after adding or renaming templates. An empty template folder cannot validate candidates. Confirm the saved cropped images are present before testing this workflow. Example cropped template: keep the full outline and minimize surrounding background.

title: Enable template refinement
text: Use AI to find candidate objects, then match reference images around those candidates. Template Matching can update the center, size, angle, or type and reject candidates without an acceptable match. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . Keep Vision AI enabled, then enable Template Matching . Select the folder under Templates . Click Open to check its images. Adjust Threshold , Scale , and Find options for the result you need. Save and apply the settings, then inspect the final detections in Dashboard. Compare object center, angle, and class with AI-only results. For AI + Template Matching, enable both switches. Select your reference-template folder and refinement options, then click Save System. The values shown are examples. Setting Effect Threshold Minimum accepted template-match score. A stricter value can reject incorrect matches but can also remove valid candidates. Scale Image reduction used during matching. For example, 0.25 means matching at one-quarter image dimensions. It does not mean the physical object is one-quarter size. Type Replace the AI class with the matched template index. Leave this off when you want to preserve AI classes. Center Use the matched template center as the object position. Size Use the matched template dimensions. Angle Use the matched template direction. For rotating parts, use an AI label type that provides a useful candidate orientation, such as ORI. The current refinement checks the candidate direction and its opposite; verify the expected angle range instead of assuming an unoriented AI box can provide every rotation. If enabling Template Matching makes valid detections disappear, check the selected folder, crop, object scale, and threshold. Verify that the final object indices still correspond to the intended destinations, especially with Type enabled.

title: Verify detection before picking
text: Keep movement tasks stopped and compare the combined result with the AI-only preview: Intended objects remain detected, while unwanted shapes fail the template check. Each accepted object has one stable detection with the expected center and orientation. Final object indices match the pick filters and destinations, especially when Type refinement is enabled. Test the positions and rotations expected during operation. Once the refined detections are reliable, continue to Pick & Place and test one object at low speed.

title: If detection does not work
text: Problem What to check All candidates disappear after matching Selected template folder, saved images, object scale, candidate direction, and threshold. Good objects are rejected Template crop and lighting; reduce the threshold gradually while checking unwanted matches. Incorrect center or angle Template alignment, AI candidate orientation, and the enabled Center/Angle options. Unexpected final type Type refinement and template filename order; recheck the destination mapping. For missing or incorrect AI detections before template refinement, use AI troubleshooting .

title: From camera images to a working model
text: Use DeltaXStudio for image capture and robot-side detection. Use AI Hub on deltaxhub.com for labeling and training. Stage What you should have before continuing Capture and download DeltaXStudio A downloaded project ZIP, extracted to an images folder on your computer. Upload and label AI Hub Images uploaded, classes defined, and every target object labeled and reviewed. Train AI Hub A completed training run for that server project. Download the model AI Hub The trained .rknn file and its class names in model order. Upload and activate DeltaXStudio The uploaded model selected, matching model type and classes entered, and settings saved. Keep the robot’s DeltaXStudio address available. Your computer needs Internet access for DeltaXHub and a connection to the robot’s network when you return to upload the model. See System Setup if the robot is still only accessible through its hotspot.

title: Capture and download images in DeltaXStudio
text: Create an image project Open the robot’s DeltaXStudio interface and select Vision in the sidebar. Set Mode to Vision AI . Beside the Project selector, click + New . Enter a descriptive name, such as sorting-parts , then click the check mark or press Enter. Confirm that the new name is selected. To add images to an existing collection, select that project instead. Open the Images tab. These images are stored on the robot controller; download them to your computer before uploading them to AI Hub. Click + New, enter a project name, and confirm with the check mark. This example enters sorting-parts. Capture representative images In the right-hand Camera Controls panel, check that the camera is connected. Set Image Type to Cropped , then click Open Live Camera . Check that the preview shows the calibrated detection area used during operation. Place objects in the detection area and click Save Current Image . Confirm that a new image appears in the list. Change the objects’ positions, rotations, and spacing before capturing the next frame. Include every class and the lighting, backgrounds, and object arrangements expected during operation. Select Cropped and open the live camera, then use Save Current Image to collect each frame. The object shown is an example. Review the saved images. Remove blurred captures, accidental duplicates, and unusable frames; check that one class or one pose does not dominate the dataset. Around 100 varied images can be a starting collection, rather than a fixed requirement. Keep some fresh captures for testing the finished model. Optional: capture a series with Auto Save With the live camera open, set Max images to the number of frames to collect and Min time (s) to the interval between saves. Enable Enable Auto Save while changing the scene between captures. Set the capture limits before enabling Auto Save. Leave automatic AIX annotation off for the first dataset. Leave Auto annotation with AIX off when preparing the first dataset. This guide labels the images in AI Hub. Turn Auto Save off when finished and review the collection before downloading it. Download and extract the images Close the live camera when capture is complete. Check the selected project, then click the download icon beside it, labeled Download project . Save the downloaded ZIP to your computer. Download the selected project with the icon immediately before + New, then extract its ZIP on your computer. In Windows, right-click the ZIP and choose Extract All . Open the extracted folder, then its images folder, and check that your captured images are present and readable. In the AI Hub steps below, upload the image files inside this folder . The project ZIP may also contain a labels folder; the image-upload button expects the images, not the ZIP or that labels folder.

title: Create a server project in DeltaXHub
text: Open deltaxhub.com and sign in. Select AI Hub → Projects → Create Project . Enter a descriptive project name and select Storage: Server . Server storage is required for the training workflow below. Local storage is for labeling and exporting data to train elsewhere. Choose the project’s label type using the table below. Leave Public off unless you intend to share the project. Click Create , then Open on the new project card. This is a separate project in DeltaXHub. Using the same name as the DeltaXStudio image project makes it easier to identify, but the images are transferred by the upload below. Open AI Hub and create a project. Select Server storage and the label type required by your application. DeltaXHub label type Meaning DeltaXStudio model type RECT A rectangular bounding box for locating an object without orientation. Suitable for simple position-based picking, such as round fruit. DET ORI An oriented bounding box for an object whose rotation matters. Label its direction consistently. ORI SEG A polygon or mask describing the object boundary, useful when the outline is important. SEG The project label type describes the annotation format. Classes describe the object categories, such as class_A and class_B ; create one class for each category the robot must distinguish. Open the newly created project to upload images and add labels.

title: Upload images and create classes
text: In the open AI Hub project, click the plus button in the left Images panel. Browse to the extracted images folder, select the captured image files, then click Open . Wait for the upload to finish and confirm the images appear in the list. Select one to check that the correct camera images were uploaded. In the right Classes panel, click plus to add the classes you need. Give them clear, consistent names. Check the class list and order before labeling. Keep a record of that order for the Objects setting on the robot. Upload captured images on the left and define object classes on the right.

title: Label and review every image
text: With an image and its intended class selected, draw a rectangle, oriented box, or segmentation outline around each target object according to the project’s label type. Check the Objects list. Correct the class of any mislabeled object and remove unwanted annotations. SAM can assist with every project label type: RECT, ORI, or SEG . It starts disabled. After selecting an image, enable SAM near the top of the editor and wait for it to become ready. First use on a new computer may take longer while the required files download. SAM needs a supported, sufficiently capable GPU; if it is unavailable, continue labeling manually. Review and correct every assisted annotation, including its box or outline, orientation where applicable, and assigned class. SAM assistance does not replace this review. Repeat for the remaining images. Review all visible target objects, including rotated or difficult examples, before starting training. Confirm the annotations are retained when you revisit an image, then click Back to leave the editor. Annotation in progress: review each outline and class, then label the remaining target objects. For ORI, keep the object’s reference direction consistent across images. For SEG, follow the actual boundary instead of including large areas of background. Assisted labeling still needs review; a plausible-looking outline can belong to the wrong class or miss part of the object.

title: Configure and start training
text: Find your server project in AI Hub’s Workspace tab and check its image and class counts. Click Train , or Retrain for a project with previous training runs. In the training dialog, select AIX New . Review Auto Configuration, or open Customize Settings to adjust the parameters. Review the displayed cost information and available credits, then click Start Training . Wait for the queued job to run and reach Completed . A queued job has not yet finished training. Start training from the project's Workspace card. Review the dataset, training configuration, and current cost information. Optional: custom training parameters Parameter What it controls Epochs The maximum number of passes through the training dataset. More epochs take longer and do not automatically improve results. The supplied example uses 100. Batch Size Images processed together in each training step. Choose a value that fits the dataset and training server memory; a larger batch is not inherently more accurate. Image Size Input resolution for training. The example uses 640 px. Higher resolution can retain small details but requires more resources. Learning Rate The size of the model’s update steps. Start with the offered default unless you have a reason to change it. Early Stopping Patience The number of epochs without sufficient improvement before training stops early. Example custom settings. Training time and credit estimates depend on the selected job. Improve dataset coverage and annotation quality before simply increasing epochs or image count. Inspect performance on fresh images as well as the reported training results.

title: Review results and download RKNN
text: Open the project’s training details and select the completed run in Training History . Inspect the training curves, class results, and confusion matrix. Check both missed objects and false detections; a high summary score alone does not verify the robot’s working conditions. Scroll to the downloads for that completed run. Click RKNN (best.rknn) and save the .rknn file on your computer. Keep it with the project name, label type, class names in model order, and training run. You will need this file and class order in DeltaXStudio. Select a completed run to inspect its results. Download the RKNN model for upload to DeltaXStudio. The Model (best.pt) download is a different format. For DeltaXStudio’s New RKNN Model upload, use the .rknn file.

title: Upload and enable the model in DeltaXStudio
text: Reconnect your computer to the robot’s network and open DeltaXStudio at its current IP address and web port, normally http://<robot-ip>:3000 . Keep movement tasks stopped while uploading and checking the model. Open Settings → System → Vision AI Settings . At New RKNN Model , click Choose File , select the downloaded .rknn file, and click Upload . Wait for the upload-success message. Select the uploaded model in Vision AI Model . Select its matching type in the adjacent dropdown: RECT → DET , ORI → ORI , or SEG → SEG . In Objects , enter all class names in the trained model’s order, separated by commas. For example, enter class_A,class_B for a model whose classes are class_A at index 0 and class_B at index 1. Do not add a trailing comma. Set the switch beside the Vision AI Settings heading to Enabled . For AI-only operation, leave Template Matching disabled. Click Save System at the top right and wait for confirmation. Uploading the file alone does not select or activate it. Return to Dashboard , open the camera view, and place a test object in the detection area. Check its class, center, and orientation before starting a movement task. If the new configuration has not taken effect after saving, use System Control → Reset , wait for reconnection, and check again. Vision AI is Enabled and Template Matching is Disabled. Select your model, type, and classes, then click Save System. The pictured model and good,bad class names are examples. Class index 0 corresponds to the first Objects entry, index 1 to the second, and so on. Keep every model class in this list even when a class should not be picked. Configure that selection under Pick Objects Index . Conf and IOU use values from 0 to 1 . Start with the provided IOU default. Increasing Conf removes lower-confidence predictions, which can also remove valid objects; it does not improve the model itself. Change one setting at a time and inspect the live result.

title: Verify detection before picking
text: Keep movement tasks stopped while checking the camera preview: Each class is detected at the positions, rotations, spacing, and partial occlusion expected during operation. Each object has one stable detection with the correct center, orientation, and class index. The empty background produces no false detections. Once detection is reliable, continue to Pick & Place and start with one object at a low test speed. To refine AI detections with reference images, continue with AI + Template Matching before testing picking.

title: Build the vision pipeline
text: Pass each result to the next block. See the Blockly program example for the block connections and test procedure. Follow these block connections and choose filter values for your objects. The values in the pictured draft are examples. Order Block Purpose 1 Get Detecting Image Read the calibrated detection image. 2 Filter HSV Keep pixels within the object’s color range. 3 Denoise Image Use morphology close/open as needed to fill small gaps and remove noise. 4 Find Contours Keep contours whose bounding-rectangle dimensions fall within the configured limits. 5 Find Rotation Objects From Contours Obtain candidate centers, sizes, and angles. 6 Match With Template Match candidates using the selected template folder. 7 Draw Rotated Objects To Image Draw the matched objects on the original detection image. 8 Convert To Tracking Object Convert the matched objects for the tracking system. 9 Push To Tracking Manager Make accepted objects available to the picking task. 10 Set Preview Image Display the annotated image for inspection. For white objects, the reference example uses lower HSV [0,0,160] and upper HSV [179,40,255] . Adjust these values to your lighting and material. The Find Contours fields are labeled Min area and Max area, but the current implementation compares both dimensions of the contour’s rotated bounding rectangle against these limits, in pixels. Set them for the object size at the current camera scale.

title: Configure Match With Template
text: Select the template folder, threshold, and match scale in the block. Connect its returned object list to both Draw Rotated Objects To Image and Convert To Tracking Object. Send this final list to tracking rather than the original color candidates. The block’s match scale is a percentage: 25% corresponds to 0.25 in System settings. The block returns the matched type, center, size, and angle, so verify template indices before assigning destinations. The System Template Matching switch stays off; this block performs the refinement. Check the program, save it, and run the vision-only task for the intended robot from Saved Tasks. Inspect the mask by temporarily using it as the preview: objects should be separated cleanly from the background, without being split into several regions or joined to their neighbors. Then restore the annotated object preview and verify one detection per object. Test similarly colored objects that should fail the template check as well as valid objects.
